akhfash:1-7.t: [He said] ﴿وَٱلْمُرْسَلاَتِ عُرْفاً﴾ ﴿فَٱلْعَاصِفَاتِ عَصْفاً﴾ ﴿وٱلنَّاشِرَاتِ نَشْراً﴾ ﴿فَٱلْفَارِقَاتِ فَرْقاً﴾ ﴿فَٱلْمُلْقِيَاتِ ذِكْراً﴾ ﴿عُذْراً أَوْ نُذْراً﴾: an oath upon ﴿إِنَّمَا تُوعَدُونَ لَوَاقِعٌ﴾ (that is, this is what is sworn to).

akhfash:8-8.t: [And He said] ﴿فَإِذَا ٱلنُّجُومُ طُمِسَتْ﴾: He left the khabar implied (unexpressed), and Allah knows best. «[Translator's note: "khabar" here means the completion of the statement, i.e., the apodosis of إذا.]»

akhfash:17-17.t: And He said ﴿ثُمَّ نُتْبِعُهُمُ ٱلآخِرِينَ﴾: nominative (indicative) because He cut it off from the first statement; and if you wish, you may make it jussive when you conjoin it to ﴿نُهْلِكِ﴾.

akhfash:25-26.t: [And] He said ﴿أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ ٱلأَرْضَ كِفَاتاً﴾ ﴿أَحْيَآءً وَأَمْواتاً﴾: as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

akhfash:27-27.t:
And He said ﴿وَأَسْقَيْنَاكُم مَّآءً فُرَاتاً﴾, that is: We made for you water from which you drink. He said ﴿وَسَقَاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ﴾ for (drinking with) the lip, and what is for the lip is without alif; [and] in a rare dialect one may also say for the lip "أَسْقَيْنةُ". «[Translator's note: so in the source; presumably أَسْقَيْتُه, "I gave him to drink".]» And Labīd said [in the wāfir metre; this is the two hundred and seventy-fifth verse cited as evidence]:
سَقَى قَوْمِي بَنِي مَجْدٍ وَأَسْقَى * نُمَيراً والقائِلَ من هِلالِ
(May He give my people, Banū Majd, to drink, and give water to Numayr and to the Qāʾil of Hilāl.)

akhfash:30-32.t: And He said ﴿إِلَىٰ ظِلٍّ ذِي ثَلاَثِ شُعَبٍ﴾ ﴿لاَّ ظَلِيلٍ وَلاَ يُغْنِي مِنَ ٱللَّهَبِ﴾, then He began anew and said ﴿إِنَّهَا تَرْمِي بِشَرَرٍ كَٱلْقَصْرِ﴾, that is: like the castles. And some read ﴿كالقَصَر﴾, that is: like the necks of camels.

akhfash:33-33.t: And He said ﴿كَأَنَّهُ جِمَالَةٌ صُفْرٌ﴾: some of the Arabs pluralise "الجِمال" (camels) [as] "الجِمالات", as you say "الجُزُرات". Some read ﴿جُمالاَتٌ﴾, and this way is not known.

akhfash:35-35.t: And He said ﴿هَـٰذَا يَوْمُ لاَ يَنطِقُونَ﴾ and made it nominative; some made it accusative, on the sense "this report is on the day they do not speak" (هذا الخبر يومَ لا ينطقون); and likewise ﴿[هَـٰذَا] يَوْمُ ٱلْفَصْلِ﴾. The tanwīn was left out because of the iḍāfa (genitive construct), as if He said "هذا يومُ لا نُطْقَ" ("this is the day of no speaking"). And if you wish, you give "day" tanwīn when you imply (a pronoun) in it, as if you said "هذا يومٌ لا يَنْطِقُون فيه" ("this is a day in which they do not speak").

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿وَالْمُرْسَلَاتِ عُرْفًا﴾ i.e. the winds, following one another like a horse's mane (ʿurf), one part following another; it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَالنَّاشِرَاتِ نَشْرًا﴾ the winds that spread the rain,

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿فَالْفَارِقَاتِ فَرْقًا﴾ i.e. the ayahs of the Quran, which distinguish between truth and falsehood and between the lawful and the unlawful,

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿فَالْمُلْقِيَاتِ ذِكْرًا﴾ i.e. the angels who descend with revelation to the prophets and messengers, who [in turn] deliver the revelation to the nations,

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿عُذْرًا أَوْ نُذْرًا﴾ i.e. for removing excuses and for warning, from Allah the Exalted; in one reading with ḍamma on the dhāl of نُذْرًا, and it has been read with ḍamma on the dhāl of عُذْرًا.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا تُوعَدُونَ﴾ i.e. the unbelievers of Mecca, of the resurrection and the punishment, ﴿لَوَاقِعٌ﴾ will happen without any doubt.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿فَإِذَا النُّجُومُ طُمِسَتْ﴾ their light is effaced,

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَإِذَا الْجِبَالُ نُسِفَتْ﴾ are crumbled and set in motion,

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿وَإِذَا الرُّسُلُ وُقِّتَتْ﴾ with wāw, and with hamza [أُقِّتَتْ] in its place, i.e. are gathered at an appointed time,

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿لِأَيِّ يَوْمٍ﴾ for a mighty day ﴿أُجِّلَتْ﴾ for bearing witness against their nations to the conveying [of the message]?

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿لِيَوْمِ الْفَصْلِ﴾ between creatures; from it the answer (jawāb) of إِذَا is taken, i.e. the judgement between creatures takes place.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا يَوْمُ الْفَصْلِ﴾ making its import awesome.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾ this is a threat to them.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿أَلَمْ نُهْلِكِ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ for their denial? I.e. We destroyed them.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿ثُمَّ نُتْبِعُهُمُ الْآخِرِينَ﴾ of those who denied, like the unbelievers of Mecca, so We destroy them.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ like what We did to the deniers ﴿نَفْعَلُ بِالْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ to everyone who commits crimes in the future, so We destroy them.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿أَلَمْ نَخْلُقْكُمْ مِنْ مَاءٍ مَهِينٍ﴾ weak, and it is semen,

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿فَجَعَلْنَاهُ فِي قَرَارٍ مَكِينٍ﴾ secure, and it is the womb,

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿إِلَى قَدَرٍ مَعْلُومٍ﴾ and it is the time of birth.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here]

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ كِفَاتًا﴾ the maṣdar (verbal noun) of كَفَتَ, meaning "to gather together", i.e. gathering together

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿أَحْيَاءً﴾ on its surface ﴿وَأَمْوَاتًا﴾ in its interior,

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا رَوَاسِيَ شَامِخَاتٍ﴾ lofty mountains ﴿وَأَسْقَيْنَاكُمْ مَاءً فُرَاتًا﴾ sweet.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾ And it is said to the deniers on the Day of Resurrection:

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿انْطَلِقُوا إِلَى مَا كُنْتُمْ بِهِ﴾ of the punishment ﴿تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿انْطَلِقُوا إِلَى ظِلٍّ ذِي ثَلَاثِ شُعَبٍ﴾ it is the smoke of Hell: when it rises it divides into three parts because of its vastness,

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿لَا ظَلِيلٍ﴾ a shelter shading them from the heat of that day ﴿وَلَا يُغْنِي﴾ wards off from them anything ﴿مِنَ اللَّهَبِ﴾ the Fire.

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿إِنَّهَا﴾ i.e. the Fire ﴿تَرْمِي بِشَرَرٍ﴾ it is what flies off from it ﴿كَالْقَصْرِ﴾ of buildings, in its size and height,

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿كَأَنَّهُ جِمَالَاتٌ﴾ plural of جِمَالَة, the plural of جَمَل; in one reading [جِمَالَةٌ]; ﴿صُفْرٌ﴾ in their shape and colour. In the hadith: "The sparks of the Fire are black like pitch (al-qīr)." The Arabs call black camels "yellow" (ṣufr) because their blackness is tinged with yellow, so it is said that ṣufr in the ayah means black for the reason mentioned, and it is said not. الشَّرَر is the plural of شَرَرَة, الشِّرَار is the plural of شَرَارَة, and الْقِير is pitch (al-qār).

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here]

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿هَذَا﴾ i.e. the Day of Resurrection ﴿يَوْمُ لَا يَنْطِقُونَ﴾ in it at all,

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿وَلَا يُؤْذَنُ لَهُمْ﴾ to excuse themselves ﴿فَيَعْتَذِرُونَ﴾ conjoined to يُؤْذَنُ without being caused by it, so it falls within the scope of the negation, i.e. there is no permission, and so no excuse.

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here]

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿هَذَا يَوْمُ الْفَصْلِ جَمَعْنَاكُمْ﴾ O deniers of this community ﴿وَالْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ of the deniers before you, so you will be reckoned and punished all together.

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿فَإِنْ كَانَ لَكُمْ كَيْدٌ﴾ a stratagem for warding off the punishment from you ﴿فَكِيدُونِ﴾ then carry it out.

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here]

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي ظِلَالٍ﴾ i.e. dense trees, since there is no sun whose heat one needs shade from, ﴿وَعُيُونٍ﴾ springing with water,

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿وَفَوَاكِهَ مِمَّا يَشْتَهُونَ﴾ in this is an announcement that food and drink in Paradise are according to their desires, unlike this world, where it is mostly according to what people find. And it is said to them:

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا هَنِيئًا﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. enjoying it with pleasure, ﴿بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ of obedience.

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿إِنَّا كَذَلِكَ﴾ just as We rewarded the God-fearing ﴿نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here]

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿كُلُوا وَتَمَتَّعُوا﴾ an address to the unbelievers in this world ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾ of time, its limit being death; in this is a threat to them; ﴿إِنَّكُمْ مُجْرِمُونَ﴾

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here]

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ارْكَعُوا﴾ pray ﴿لَا يَرْكَعُونَ﴾ they do not pray.

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here]

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ حَدِيثٍ بَعْدَهُ﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ i.e. their believing in any other of Allah's books after denying it is not possible, because it contains the inimitability that no other contains.

daas-irab:16-19.t: ﴿أَلَمْ نُهْلِكِ﴾: the hamza is an interrogative particle, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction; ﴿نُتْبِعُهُمُ﴾: an imperfect verb and its first object, the agent being latent; ﴿الْآخِرِينَ﴾: a second direct object; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿نَفْعَلُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is latent; ﴿بِالْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is resumptive. The i'rab of the verse after it has already been given.

daas-irab:20-24.t: ﴿أَلَمْ نَخْلُقْكُمْ﴾: the hamza is an interrogative particle, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam; the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿مِنْ ماءٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿مَهِينٍ﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَجَعَلْناهُ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb with its agent and its object; ﴿فِي قَرارٍ﴾: attached to the verb; ﴿مَكِينٍ﴾: an adjective; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِلى قَدَرٍ﴾: attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿مَعْلُومٍ﴾: adjective of قدر. ﴿فَقَدَرْنا﴾: a past verb and its agent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَنِعْمَ﴾: a past verb for expressing praise; ﴿الْقادِرُونَ﴾: its agent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. The i'rab of the verse after it has already been given.

daas-irab:25-28.t: ﴿أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ﴾: the hamza is an interrogative particle, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿الْأَرْضَ﴾: first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿كِفاتاً﴾: second direct object; the clause is resumptive; ﴿أَحْياءً﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿وَأَمْواتاً﴾: conjoined to أحياء. ﴿وَجَعَلْنا﴾: a past verb and its agent; ﴿فِيها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿رَواسِيَ﴾: direct object; ﴿شامِخاتٍ﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَأَسْقَيْناكُمْ﴾: a past verb, its agent and its first object; ﴿ماءً﴾: second direct object; ﴿فُراتاً﴾: adjective; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. The i'rab of the one following it has already been given.

daas-irab:29-34.t: ﴿انْطَلِقُوا﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the maqūl (speech content) of an omitted verb of saying; ﴿إِلى ما﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾: kāna and its noun; ﴿بِهِ﴾: attached to what follows it; ﴿تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, the wāw being its agent; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of كنتم, and the clause كنتم… is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿انْطَلِقُوا﴾: an imperative verb and its agent; the clause is a badal (substitute) for the preceding one; ﴿إِلى ظِلٍّ﴾: attached to the verb; ﴿ذِي﴾: naʿt (adjective) of ظل, muḍāf to ﴿ثَلاثِ﴾; and ﴿شُعَبٍ﴾ is also muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لا﴾: negative; ﴿ظَلِيلٍ﴾: a second adjective of ظل. ﴿وَ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿لا﴾: negative; ﴿يُغْنِي﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is latent (mustatir); ﴿مِنَ اللَّهَبِ﴾: attached to the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّها﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿تَرْمِي﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is latent; the clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is resumptive; ﴿بِشَرَرٍ﴾: attached to the verb; ﴿كَالْقَصْرِ﴾: adjective of شرر. ﴿كَأَنَّهُ جِمالَتٌ﴾: its noun and its predicate; ﴿صُفْرٌ﴾: adjective of جمالة; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). The i'rab of the verse after it has already been given.

daas-irab:35-37.t: ﴿هذا يَوْمُ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive. ﴿لا﴾: negative; ﴿يَنْطِقُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿وَ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿لا﴾: negative; ﴿يُؤْذَنُ﴾: a passive imperfect verb, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿لَهُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿فَيَعْتَذِرُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its agent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. The i'rab of the following verse has already been given.

daas-irab:38-40.t: ﴿هذا يَوْمُ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); ﴿الْفَصْلِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is the maqūl (speech content) of an omitted verb of saying. ﴿جَمَعْناكُمْ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَ﴾: the wāw is the wāw of accompaniment (maʿiyya); ﴿الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾: mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment). ﴿فَإِنْ﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and ﴿إن﴾ is a conditional particle that puts the verb in the jussive; ﴿كانَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb; ﴿لَكُمْ﴾: the fronted khabar of kāna; ﴿كَيْدٌ﴾: its postponed noun; ﴿فَكِيدُونِ﴾: the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ (rābiṭa), and an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its agent, the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), and the omitted yāʾ of the first person is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). The following verse: its i'rab has already been given.

daas-irab:41-45.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿فِي ظِلالٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of inna; the clause is resumptive; ﴿وَعُيُونٍ﴾: conjoined to ظلال. ﴿وَفَواكِهَ﴾: also conjoined; ﴿مِمَّا﴾: attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of فواكه; ﴿يَشْتَهُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿كُلُوا﴾: an imperative verb and its agent; the clause is the maqūl (speech content) of an omitted verb of saying; ﴿وَاشْرَبُوا﴾: conjoined to كلوا; ﴿هَنِيئاً﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿بِما﴾: attached to هنيئا; ﴿كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾: kāna and its noun, and an imperfect verb in the nominative, the wāw being its agent; the clause is the khabar of كنتم, and the clause كنتم is the ṣila of ما. ﴿إِنَّا﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾: adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿نَجْزِي﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is latent (mustatir); ﴿الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the khabar of إنا, and the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīl). The i'rab of the verse after it has already been given.

daas-irab:46-47.t: ﴿كُلُوا﴾: an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the maqūl (speech content) of an omitted verb of saying; ﴿وَتَمَتَّعُوا﴾: conjoined to كلوا. ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾: in the position of an accusative as an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān); ﴿إِنَّكُمْ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿مُجْرِمُونَ﴾: its khabar (predicate); the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīl) for the command and has no grammatical position. The i'rab of the verse after it has already been given.

daas-irab:48-50.t: ﴿وَإِذا﴾: the wāw is a resumptive particle; ﴿إِذا﴾ is a conditional adverb that does not put the verb in the jussive; ﴿قِيلَ﴾: a passive past verb; ﴿لَهُمُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿ارْكَعُوا﴾: an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the maqūl (speech content) of the saying; ﴿لا﴾: negative; ﴿يَرْكَعُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its agent; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position. The i'rab of the verse following it has already been given. ﴿فَبِأَيِّ﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ indicating an implied condition), and ﴿بأي﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يؤمنون; ﴿حَدِيثٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿بَعْدَهُ﴾: an adverb of time; ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative, the wāw being its agent; the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:1-7.t:
﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a particle of oath and a preposition. ﴿الْمُرْسَلاتِ﴾ that by which the oath is sworn (muqsam bihi), genitive (majrūr); the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb of oath; and ﴿عُرْفاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَالْعاصِفاتِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to المرسلات; and ﴿عَصْفاً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿وَالنَّاشِراتِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it; and ﴿نَشْراً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq. ﴿فَالْفارِقاتِ﴾ also conjoined; and ﴿فَرْقاً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq. ﴿فَالْمُلْقِياتِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it by the fāʾ; and ﴿ذِكْراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of الملقيات. And ﴿عُذْراً﴾ mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿أَوْ نُذْراً﴾ conjoined to عذرا by aw.
﴿إن﴾ a particle resembling the verb; and ﴿ما﴾ its noun; and ﴿تُوعَدُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿لَواقِعٌ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa). ﴿واقع﴾ khabar (predicate) of inna; the nominal clause is the response to an oath (jawāb qasam), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:8-15.t: ﴿فَإِذَا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle; and ﴿إذا﴾ a conditional adverb of time that does not make jussive; and ﴿النُّجُومُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of an omitted verb explained by the one mentioned; and ﴿طُمِسَتْ﴾ a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is explicative (mufassira) of the implied conditional clause, and the condition with its apodosis is resumptive, and what follows is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it. ﴿لِأَيِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb after them; and ﴿يَوْمٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and ﴿أُجِّلَتْ﴾ a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil is latent; the clause is the object of an omitted saying (maqūl qawl maḥdhūf); and ﴿لِيَوْمِ﴾ badal (substitute) of أيّ; and ﴿الْفَصْلِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَما﴾ an interrogative noun as mubtadaʾ (subject); and ﴿أَدْراكَ﴾ a past verb and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it; and ﴿ما يَوْمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; and ﴿الْفَصْلِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause stands in place of the second object of أدراك; and ﴿وَيْلٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ; and ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ an adverb annexed to its like; and ﴿لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾ khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is resumptive.

dervis-irab:1-19.t:
* I'rab:
(وَالْمُرْسَلاتِ عُرْفاً) Abū Ḥayyān said in al-Nahr: «This sūra is Meccan, and its connection with what precedes it is very clear: He mentioned that He, the Exalted, has mercy on whom He wills and punishes the wrongdoers, and this is a true promise from Him; so He swore to its occurrence and said إن ما توعدون لواقع. And since the things sworn by are qualified nouns that have been omitted, their attributes being put in their place, there arose disagreement about those qualified nouns. What appears is that the things sworn by are two, and for this reason the conjunction came with the wāw in والناشرات, and conjunction with the wāw signals difference; whereas conjunction with the fāʾ, when it is among attributes, indicates that they go back to a single qualified noun. Once this is established, the apparent meaning is that He swore first by the winds, which is indicated by the conjunction of the attribute with the fāʾ; and the second oath contains an ascent to something nobler than the first thing sworn by, namely the angels; and His saying فالفارقات فالملقيات is among their attributes, and their casting of the Reminder, which is what Allah the Exalted sent down, is properly attributed to them. And what is mentioned of the exegetes' disagreement about what is meant by these attributes should be taken as illustration, not specification. The answer to the oath and what is conjoined to it is إن ما توعدون; ما is a relative noun meaning الذي, and the referent pronoun is omitted, i.e. إن الذي توعدونه; it is the noun of إنّ, and His saying لواقع is its khabar (predicate).» We have prefaced with this useful glimpse to clarify the truth and to ward off the confusion that may arise from the exegetes' disagreement, and after it we return to the parsing. The wāw is for the oath; المرسلات is genitive (majrūr) by the wāw of the oath, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, implied as «I swear». As for عرفا, either it is from ʿurf al-faras (with ḍamma on the ʿayn), i.e. the hair of a horse's neck, in which case it is parsed as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun concealed in المرسلات, the meaning being by way of simile, i.e. in the state of being ʿurf, i.e. resembling a horse's mane in their succession and following one another as it does; or it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), as if He said: by those sent forth in a sending, i.e. in succession. Or it is from al-ʿurf, which is kindness (al-maʿrūf), in the manner of the saying of al-Ḥuṭayʾa:
من يفعل الخير لا يعدم جوازيه ... لا يذهب العرف بين الله والناس
(Whoever does good will not lack its recompense; kindness is not lost between Allah and people.)
And it is accusative (manṣūb) as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. they were sent for beneficence and kindness, or accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ). (فَالْعاصِفاتِ عَصْفاً) The fāʾ is a conjunction for immediate sequence; العاصفات is conjoined to المرسلات, and it is an active participle from al-ʿaṣf in the sense of intensity. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «The wind ʿaṣafat, ʿaṣfan, of the pattern of ḍaraba, and also ʿuṣūfan: it became violent.» And عصفا is an emphasizing maṣdar, so it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). (وَالنَّاشِراتِ نَشْراً فَالْفارِقاتِ فَرْقاً فَالْمُلْقِياتِ ذِكْراً) الناشرات is also conjoined, and نشرا is an absolute object; فالفارقات is also conjoined, and فرقا is an absolute object; فالملقيات is also conjoined, and ذكرا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of الملقيات, i.e. of the angels who descend with the revelation to the prophets. (عُذْراً أَوْ نُذْراً) These are two maṣdars: from ʿadhara, when one effaces wrongdoing, and from andhara, when one warns against disbelief, like kufr and shukr. They are accusative as objects of purpose. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed them to be accusative as a badal (substitute) of ذكرا. And Abū al-Baqāʾ's wording:
«In عذرا أو نذرا there are two aspects. One: they are two maṣdars whose middle letter may be quiescent or take ḍamma. The second: they are plurals of ʿadhīr and nadhīr. On the first, they are accusative as objects of purpose or as a substitute of ذكرا; on the second, they are two ḥāls of the pronoun in الملقيات, i.e. excusing and warning.» (إِنَّما تُوعَدُونَ لَواقِعٌ) The clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath. إنّ is a particle resembling the verb; ما is a relative noun, the noun of إنّ; the clause توعدون is the ṣila (relative clause); the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) and واقع is the predicate of إنّ; the referent pronoun is omitted, i.e. إن الذي توعدونه. (فَإِذَا النُّجُومُ طُمِسَتْ) The fāʾ is resumptive; إذا is a future adverb containing the sense of condition; النجوم is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of an omitted verb explained by what follows, and the clause طمست is explicative, with no grammatical position. On the apodosis (jawāb) of إذا there are two views. One is that it is omitted, its implied form being «when the stars are effaced, what you are promised will occur», as indicated by His saying إنما توعدون لواقع. The second is that it is لأي يوم أجلت, on the implication of a saying, i.e. «it will be said: for what day were they deferred?», so the verb (of saying) is in reality the apodosis. The meaning of طمست is: erased and obliterated, and their light gone. (وَإِذَا السَّماءُ فُرِجَتْ وَإِذَا الْجِبالُ نُسِفَتْ وَإِذَا الرُّسُلُ أُقِّتَتْ) Clauses conjoined to the clause فإذا النجوم طمست. The meaning of فرجت is: opened, so that it became gates. The meaning of نسفت is: crumbled like flowing sand, then the wind carries it away. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «The wind nasafat the dust, nasfan, of the pattern of ḍaraba: it uprooted it and scattered it.» The meaning of أقتت is وقتت, and it was read with both, i.e. gathered for a known time. Al-Zajjāj said: what is meant by this taʾqīt or tawqīt is the clarification of the time in which they will be brought to bear witness against their nations; and the wāw, when it takes a ḍamma, may be made a hamza. Al-Mubarrad said in his Kāmil: «Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: وإذا الرسل أقتت, and the origin is وقتت; were it outside the Qurʾān, it would be permissible to make the wāw overt if you wished.» (لِأَيِّ يَوْمٍ أُجِّلَتْ، لِيَوْمِ الْفَصْلِ) لأي يوم is attached to أجلت, i.e. أجلت لأي يوم. The clause is the speech of an omitted saying, in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of the nominative of أقتت, i.e. «it being said: for what day were they deferred?»; or it has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of إذا, as has preceded. ليوم الفصل is a substitute of لأي يوم with repetition of the governing element; you may also attach it to an omitted verb, i.e. «they were deferred for the Day of Decision». (وَما أَدْراكَ ما يَوْمُ الْفَصْلِ) The wāw is a conjunction; ما is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause أدراك is its predicate, and the kāf is the first direct object. His saying ما يوم الفصل is a clause of a subject, namely the interrogative ما, and a predicate, namely يوم الفصل, standing in place of the second object of إدراك, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative. The first interrogative means deeming far-fetched and disapproval, and the second is for magnification and making terrible. (وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ) ويل is a subject; what licensed beginning with it is the sense of imprecation in it. Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: «If you say: how did the indefinite noun occur as a subject in His saying ويل يومئذ للمكذبين? I say: in its origin it is an accusative maṣdar standing in place of its verb, but it was diverted to the nominative to indicate the fixity and permanence of the meaning of destruction for those imprecated against; similar is سلام عليكم. ويلا in the accusative is permissible, but it was not read so.» يومئذ is an adverb annexed to its like, and it is attached to ويل or is an adjective of it; the nunation is a substitute for omitted clauses taken from the context, the implied form being «on the day when stars are effaced and what follows it occurs». للمكذبين is the predicate of ويل. (أَلَمْ نُهْلِكِ الْأَوَّلِينَ ثُمَّ نُتْبِعُهُمُ الْآخِرِينَ) The hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī), because the interrogative is in origin one of disapproval, and it has entered upon a negation, and the negation of a negation is an affirmation, and this is expressed as the interrogative of affirmation. لم is a particle of negation, conversion (to past) and jussive; نهلك is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as «We»; الأولين is the direct object. ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay; نتبعهم is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) as a resumption, i.e. «then We will make them followed»; and الآخرين is a second direct object. (كَذلِكَ نَفْعَلُ بِالْمُجْرِمِينَ، وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ) كذلك is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. «like that hideous action We do»; بالمجرمين is attached to نفعل. The parsing of ويل يومئذ للمكذبين has preceded, and the secret of its repetition will come in the section on rhetoric.

* Rhetoric:
The verse «ويل يومئذ للمكذبين» is repeated in this sūra ten times, and the secret in it is the increase of intimidation. Repetition in the context of encouragement and intimidation is acceptable and fine, especially when the verses preceding the repeated occurrences differ, as here.

* Benefits:
It is not permissible to conjoin «نتبعهم» to «نهلك», because the conjunction would require that it be «We destroyed the former peoples», since لم is a particle of negation, conversion (to past) and jussive; so the meaning would be «then We made the later ones follow them in destruction», and the matter is not so, because the destruction of the later ones has not yet occurred.

dervis-irab:20-34.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فَقَدَرْنا) Without doubling, from al-qudra (power); and it was read with doubling, from al-taqdīr (measuring/ordaining). The first is indicated by فنعم القادرون. In al-Qurṭubī: «Nāfiʿ and al-Kisāʾī read فقدّرنا with doubling, and the rest read it light; they are two dialectal forms with the meaning of فقدرنا without doubling.» In al-Miṣbāḥ: «I qadartu the thing, qadran, of the patterns of ḍaraba and qatala, and qaddartuhu, taqdīran, with the same meaning; and the noun is al-qadar, with two fatḥas.» And his saying ﷺ فاقدروا له means: reckon the number of the month, so complete Shaʿbān as thirty days.
(كِفاتاً) Al-Jalāl said: «a maṣdar (verbal noun) of kafata in the sense of gathering together.» He said in al-Qāmūs:
«kafatahu, yakfituhu: he turned him away from his direction, so he was turned away; and the thing to himself: he gathered it and drew it in, like kaffatahu; and the bird and other things, kaftan, kifātan, kafītan and kafatānan: it sped in flying and running.» So is كفاتا the maṣdar of the transitive kafata in the sense of «gathered», or the maṣdar of the intransitive kafata of the bird?! The words of the author of al-Qāmūs are misleading. After that he said in al-Qāmūs: «And al-kifāt (with kasra) is the place in which a thing is gathered, i.e. drawn together and collected; and the earth is a kifāt for us.» Al-Zamakhsharī and Abū Ḥayyān followed this. The exegetes refuted al-Jalāl because kafata is of the pattern of ḍaraba; so the truth is that it is a noun of place. In al-Mukhtār: «kafatahu: he drew it to himself, of the pattern of ḍaraba; and al-kifāt (with kasra) is the place in which a thing is gathered, i.e. drawn together and collected; and the earth is a kifāt for us.» And al-Samīn's wording: «al-kifāt is a name for the container in which a thing is gathered, i.e. collected; one says kafatahu, yakfituhu, i.e. he collected it and drew it together», until he said: «and it is said كفاتا is a plural of kāfit, like ṣiyām and qiyām as plurals of ṣāʾim and qāʾim; and it is said rather that it is a maṣdar like al-kitāb and al-ḥisāb.» More of this exposition will come in the section on i'rab.
(كَالْقَصْرِ) [i.e. like the palace,] of buildings, in its hugeness and height.
(جِمالَتٌ) With kasra on the jīm, the plural of jamal (camel), and the tāʾ is for the feminine of the plural. One says jamal, jimāl and jimāla, like dhakar, dhikār and dhikāra, and ḥajar, ḥijār and ḥijāra. It is said that it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ), like al-dhikāra and al-ḥijāra. And جمالات was read; it may be a plural of jimāla, or a plural of jimāl, so that it is a plural of a plural; and it may be a plural of jamal, as in the saying رجالات قريش. More of this exposition will come in the section on rhetoric.

* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ نَخْلُقْكُمْ مِنْ ماءٍ مَهِينٍ) The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval and affirmation; لم is a particle of negation, conversion (to past) and jussive; نخلقكم is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as «We»; the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); من ماء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) نخلقكم, and مهين is a naʿt (adjective) of ماء. The من of beginning is an indication that He, the Exalted, is able to originate, and whoever is able to originate is able to restore. (فَجَعَلْناهُ فِي قَرارٍ مَكِينٍ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; جعلناه is a verb, its agent and its direct object; في قرار is in the place of the second object, and مكين is an adjective of قرار, i.e. a place in which the semen is preserved from the harms that would spoil it, such as air; and the قرار is the womb. (إِلى قَدَرٍ مَعْلُومٍ) إلى قدر: the preposition and its genitive noun are in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. deferred to a known measure; معلوم is an adjective of قدر. (فَقَدَرْنا فَنِعْمَ الْقادِرُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; قدرنا is a verb and its agent; the fāʾ is a conjunction; نعم is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing praise; القادرون is the agent, and the one specified for praise is omitted, i.e. «We». (وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ) Its parsing has preceded. (أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ كِفاتاً أَحْياءً وَأَمْواتاً) The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval and affirmation; لم is a particle of negation, conversion and jussive; نجعل is an imperfect verb, jussive by لم, its agent latent, implied as «We»; الأرض is the first direct object and كفاتا the second direct object of نجعل, because it is for transformation (taṣyīr). أحياء and أمواتا are accusative as two direct objects of كفاتا, if it is established that كفاتا is a maṣdar, or a plural of kāfit, since that is an active participle. If it is not a maṣdar but a noun of place, then their accusative is by an implied verb indicated by كفاتا, its implied form being «it gathers», the meaning being: it gathers the living on its back and the dead in its belly. Abū Ḥayyān's wording:
«أحياء and أمواتا are accusative by a verb indicated by what precedes, i.e. it gathers the living on its back and the dead in its belly.» And al-Zamakhsharī said: «It is possible that the meaning be: it gathers you living and dead, so that they are accusative as ḥāls of the pronoun, because it is known that it is the gathering-place of humankind.» (وَجَعَلْنا فِيها رَواسِيَ شامِخاتٍ وَأَسْقَيْناكُمْ ماءً فُراتاً) The wāw is a conjunction; جعلنا is a verb and its agent; فيها is attached to جعلنا if it means «We created», and is in the place of the second object if جعلنا means «We made (into)». رواسي is the object of جعلنا and شامخات an adjective of رواسي. أسقيناكم is conjoined to جعلنا; ماء is the second object and فراتا an adjective of ماء; al-furāt is sweet water. (وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ) Its parsing has preceded. (انْطَلِقُوا إِلى ما كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تُكَذِّبُونَ) The clause is the speech of an omitted, resumed saying. انطلقوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; إلى ما is attached to انطلقوا; the clause كنتم has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما; كان and its noun; به is attached to تكذبون; the clause تكذبون is the khabar (predicate) of كنتم, and the referent pronoun is the pronoun in به. (انْطَلِقُوا إِلى ظِلٍّ ذِي ثَلاثِ شُعَبٍ) انطلقوا is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the first انطلقوا; إلى ظل is attached to انطلقوا, and ذي ثلاث شعب is an adjective of ظل. More of this meaning will come in the section on rhetoric. (لا ظَلِيلٍ وَلا يُغْنِي مِنَ اللَّهَبِ) لا is negative, and ظليل is a negated adjective, because shade is never anything but shading; so negating it of it indicates that He called it shade in mockery and derision of them. ولا يغني من اللهب is conjoined to the negated element; يغني is an imperfect verb whose agent is «it», the shade; من اللهب is attached to يغني; and the clause is in the position of the genitive, i.e. not availing them anything against the heat of the flame. (إِنَّها تَرْمِي بِشَرَرٍ كَالْقَصْرِ) The clause stands as a causal explanation of the non-availing of the non-shading shade. إنّ and its noun, the pronoun referring to Jahannam, because the talk is about it; the clause ترمي is the predicate of إنّ; بشرر is attached to ترمي. al-sharar is what flies off from it; you say: a fire with sharār and sharar, and a sharāra and a sharara flew off from it. كالقصر is an adjective of شرر, i.e. every spark is like a qaṣr, of palaces, in its hugeness. More of this simile will come in the section on rhetoric. (كَأَنَّهُ جِمالَتٌ صُفْرٌ) The clause is a second adjective of شرر; كأنّ and its noun; جمالة is its predicate and صفر an adjective of جمالة. (وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ) Its parsing has preceded.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «أحياء وأمواتا» there is indefiniteness: He made them indefinite, although it gathers all the living and the dead, for magnification, as if it were said: living ones beyond counting and dead ones beyond reckoning; besides which, the living and dead of humankind are not all the living and the dead.
2- And He made رواسي شامخات and ماء فراتا indefinite to convey partition, because in the sky there are mountains — Allah the Exalted said: «وينزل من السماء من جبال فيها من برد» — and in it there is much sweet water; indeed it is its source and its outflow.
3- In His saying: «انطلقوا إلى ظل ذي ثلاث شعب، لا ظليل ولا يغني من اللهب» there is a curious art among the arts of rhetoric, which the ancients named «al-ʿunwān» (the title/index). Reference to it has preceded in this book: it consists in the speaker taking up a purpose of his — description, boasting, praise, reproach, satire or other such arts — and then, with the aim of completing it, bringing examples of words that serve as a title for earlier reports and past stories. And there is a very great kind of it, which is what serves as a title for the sciences: that words are mentioned in the speech which serve as keys to sciences and entrances to them. This verse we are dealing with is among the truest proofs of that, for His saying «ظل ذي ثلاث شعب» is a title for the science attributed to Euclid, a Greek philosopher who composed a book on astronomy, geometry and arithmetic, which al-Ḥajjāj ibn Yūsuf al-Kūfī translated into Arabic. He taught geometry in Alexandria in the days of Ptolemy and laid down the principles of plane geometry; he also has the book of the Elements, which Nāṣir al-Dīn al-Ṭūsī commented upon; and he died in the year 283. [Translator's note: translated as written; it is unclear in the source to whom the death date refers, and the details are compressed.] For the triangular figure is the first of figures and their basis, and from it the rest of the figures are composed; and it is a figure which, when set up in the sun, however it is set up and on whichever of its sides, has no shade, because of the sharpness of the vertices of its angles. So Allah, Glorified is He, commanded these people of Hell to go off to the shade of this figure in mockery and derision of them.
4- Simile (tashbīh): He, Glorified is He, likened the sparks to the palace in its hugeness and size, and likened them secondly to yellow camels in form, colour, multitude, succession and speed of movement. We quote here a curious passage of al-Zamakhsharī and then comment on it briefly. He said in al-Kashshāf: «They were likened to palaces and then to camels to make the simile clear; do you not see that they liken camels to al-afdān and al-majādil?» — i.e. palaces, the plural of fadan and mijdal, both meaning palace, as in al-Ṣiḥāḥ. Then he said: «And جمالات was read with ḍamma, which are the thick ropes (qulūs) of bridges; and it is said the ropes of sea ships, the singular being jumāla» — and al-qulūs is the plural of qals, a thick rope among the ropes of ships. Then he said: «And it is said: صفر, intending the genus; and it is said: صفر means black ones tending to yellowness. And in the poetry of ʿImrān ibn Ḥiṭṭān the Khārijite:
دعتهم بأعلى صوتها ورمتهم ... بمثل الجمال الصفر نزاعة للشوى
(It called them with its loudest voice and pelted them with the like of yellow camels, stripping away the scalps.)
And Abū al-ʿAlāʾ said:
حمراء ساطعة الذوائب في الدجى ... ترمي بكل شرارة كطراف
(Red, its locks shining in the darkness, it throws every spark like a leather tent.)
So he likened it to the ṭirāf, which is a tent of leather, in hugeness and redness. It is as though, out of his malice, he intended to go beyond the simile of the Qurʾān; and in his conceit at the illusion of surpassing it that he was tempted into, he placed at the beginning of his verse his word «حمراء» as a preparation for it, a proclamation of it, and an alerting of the listeners to its place. But he was blind — may Allah join for him the blindness of both abodes — to His saying, Mighty and Majestic: «كأنه جمالات صفر», for that is equivalent to saying «like a red tent». Moreover, in the simile with the qaṣr, which is the fortress, there is a likening from two aspects: hugeness and height in the air; and in the simile with jumālāt, which are the ropes, there is a likening from three aspects: hugeness, length and yellowness. So may Allah render far his strangeness in his ṭirāf, and the cheeks he puffed out in finding it so original.»
And the author of Nasmat al-Saḥar mentioned, concerning al-Zamakhsharī at His saying, the Exalted:
«إنها ترمي بشرر كالقصر», that he mentioned the verse of Abū al-ʿAlāʾ describing the fire of hospitality, from the qaṣīda rhyming in fāʾ in which he elegized the Naqīb Abū Aḥmad al-Mūsawī, father of al-Sharīf al-Raḍī and al-Murtaḍā, namely:
حمراء ساطعة الذوائب في الدجى ... ترمي بكلّ شرارة كطراف
and he became heated against him and said that he intended and aimed to go beyond the simile of the Mighty Qurʾān with the palace. He said: «And I do not know whence he got that he aimed to go beyond the simile of the Qurʾān, for it is known that the palace is greater than the ṭirāf, which is a tent of red leather used by the nomadic Turks and the wealthy among the Arabs; but al-Zamakhsharī, despite his merit, was very sharp of temper.»
I say: al-Zamakhsharī — may Allah have mercy on him — picks quarrels with Abū al-ʿAlāʾ in many places, and he is, as we see in his criticism of al-Maʿarrī's beautiful verse, clearly biased and partial. We are accustomed to al-Zamakhsharī attacking the opponents of the Muʿtazila, and Abū al-ʿAlāʾ was not one of them; but al-Zamakhsharī was a man of letters who had read al-Maʿarrī's epistles and took note of his stance toward the grammarians, so his dislike drove him to provoke him.
This grammatical feud did harm to Abū al-ʿAlāʾ, for the grammarians neglected his poetry and very rarely took it up with commentary, citation or criticism; they gave attention to the poetry of Abū Tammām and al-Mutanabbī for their free handling of the language and of grammatical styles, and there was in Abū al-ʿAlāʾ's poetry what would tempt them to study it, but they turned away from it. Al-Maʿarrī's criticism of the grammarians has passed in this book, so renew your acquaintance with it.
As for likening camels to al-afdān, which are palaces, it is very frequent in their poetry. ʿAntara said:
فوقفت فيها ناقتي فكأنها ... فدن لأقضي حاجة المتلوم
(I halted my she-camel there, and she was like a castle, so that I might fulfil the need of one who lingers.)
And al-Maʿarrī was captivated by the description of camels and tried to follow in their footsteps, but he went extremely far into strangeness in that, as in his saying, from a qaṣīda of his in Saqṭ al-Zand addressing the keeper of the House of Knowledge in Baghdad:
وحرف كدال تحت ميم ولم يكن ... براء يؤم الرسم غيره النقط
(And a lean she-camel like a dāl beneath a mīm, and there was no "rāʾ" heading for the trace that the drops had altered.)
The ḥarf is the she-camel, and the dāl is a likening of it; the mīm is the bent-over rider, from the angle of simile, not of lexical explanation; the rāʾī is one who strikes the lung, from raʾāhu when he hits his lung; the rasm is the trace of the abodes, and al-nuqaṭ is rain. We have digressed to this only to set out al-Maʿarrī's strangeness, in criticism of which al-Zamakhsharī did not go beyond the truth.

dervis-irab:35-50.t:
* I'rab:
(هذا يَوْمُ لا يَنْطِقُونَ وَلا يُؤْذَنُ لَهُمْ فَيَعْتَذِرُونَ) A resumed statement, presented to set out the state on that day. هذا is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and يوم its khabar (predicate); the clause لا ينطقون is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. It was also read with a fatḥa on the mīm, being accusative as an adverb, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted predicate of هذا. The wāw is a conjunction; لا is negative; يؤذن is an imperfect verb, passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), implied as «it»; لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يؤذن. The fāʾ is a conjunction, and يعتذرون is an imperfect verb conjoined to يؤذن, included in the string of the negation without being caused by it; for this reason it was not made accusative, because had it been made accusative it would inevitably have been caused by it. Al-Samīn's wording: «In the nominative of فيعتذرون there are two aspects. One is that it is resumed, i.e. فهم يعتذرون. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: and the meaning would be that they do not speak with a speech that benefits them, or that they speak at some stations and do not speak at others. The second is that it is conjoined to يؤذن, so it is negated; and had it been made accusative, it would have been caused by it.» Al-Bayḍāwī said: He conjoined يعتذرون to يؤذن to indicate the negation of permission and of excuse-making following it absolutely; had He made it an answer, it would have indicated that their not making excuses is because of the lack of permission, and that would have given the false impression that they have an excuse but were not permitted to give it. (وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ) Its parsing has preceded. (هذا يَوْمُ الْفَصْلِ جَمَعْناكُمْ وَالْأَوَّلِينَ) The clause is the speech of an omitted saying, i.e. «and it is said to them: this...». هذا is the subject and يوم الفصل its predicate; the clause جمعناكم is explicative, clarifying His saying هذا يوم الفصل, because if it is the Day of Decision between the blessed and the wretched and between the prophets and their nations, then the former and the latter must be gathered so that this decision may take place between them. The wāw is a conjunction or for accompaniment, and الأولين is conjoined to the kāf or is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment). (فَإِنْ كانَ لَكُمْ كَيْدٌ فَكِيدُونِ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; إن is conditional; كان is a deficient past verb; لكم is its fronted predicate and كيد its delayed noun. The fāʾ connects the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) because it is a request clause; كيدون is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the nūn is for protection (al-wiqāya), and the omitted yāʾ of the speaker is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ) Its parsing has preceded. (إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي ظِلالٍ وَعُيُونٍ) A resumed statement, presented to mention the states of the believers concisely after He mentioned the states of the disbelievers at length, so as to complete the balance between this sūra and the sūra before it, namely هل أتى على الإنسان; for in that sūra He mentioned the states of the disbelievers concisely and was lengthy in mentioning the states of the believers. إنّ and its noun; في ظلال is its predicate and عيون is conjoined to ظلال. (وَفَواكِهَ مِمَّا يَشْتَهُونَ) Conjoined to ظلال and عيون; مما is a naʿt (adjective) of فواكه, and the clause يشتهون has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila (relative clause). (كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا هَنِيئاً بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ)
The clause is the speech of an omitted saying, and this saying is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun of المتقين in the adverbial phrase في ظلال, i.e. they are settled in shades, that being said to them. The parsing of هنيئا has preceded many times, i.e. a ḥāl, i.e. enjoying it wholesomely. بما is attached to هنيئا; the bāʾ is causal and ما is a relative noun; the clause كنتم is the ṣila; كان and its noun, and the clause تعملون its predicate. (إِنَّا كَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ) A causal explanation of the command to eat and drink, i.e. that is Our custom and habit: We reward the doer of good for his good just as We requite the evildoer for his evil. إنّ and its noun; كذلك is a fronted adjective of an omitted maṣdar; the clause نجزي is the predicate of إنّا, and المحسنين is the direct object. (وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ) Its parsing has preceded. (كُلُوا وَتَمَتَّعُوا قَلِيلًا إِنَّكُمْ مُجْرِمُونَ) The clause is the speech of an omitted saying, and this omitted element is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of المكذبين, i.e. woe is fixed for them in the state of its being said to them: eat and enjoy yourselves. كلوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the omission of the nūn, and تمتعوا is conjoined to it. قليلا is accusative as an adverb of time — a time that does not tarry before it ends with your death and perishing; and in any case, however long it extends and is prolonged, it is little and passing, near and hastening, when measured against the spans of the Hereafter and its long days. The clause إنكم مجرمون is a causal explanation of the threat understood from the command to eat and enjoy a shade that passes, a colour that fades, and a deceptive mirage. إنّ and its noun, and مجرمون its predicate. The wording of al-Kashshāf: «If you say: how is it valid that this be said to them in the Hereafter? I say: it is said to them in the Hereafter as an announcement that in the world they deserved that it be said to them, and that they were worthy of it, as a reminder of their ugly state and of what they brought upon themselves by preferring little enjoyment to everlasting bliss and kingdom. In its manner is the saying:
إخوتي لا تبعدوا أبدا ... وبلى والله قد بعدوا
(My brothers, may you never be far — and yes, by Allah, they have gone far.)
He means: you deserved in your lifetime that this be prayed for you. And He gave as the reason for that their being criminals, as an indication that every criminal has nothing but eating and enjoyment for a few days, then remaining in destruction forever. And it is possible that كلوا وتمتعوا be a resumed statement addressed to the deniers in the world» — i.e. so it would go back to what precedes His saying إن المتقين. Al-Jalāl took this view, and al-Qurṭubī and Abū Ḥayyān supported it. (وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ) Its parsing has preceded. (وَإِذا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ارْكَعُوا لا يَرْكَعُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction connected with His saying للمكذبين, as if it were said: woe to those who denied and to those who, when it is said to them «bow», ...; or with His saying إنكم مجرمون by way of iltifāt (shift of person), as if it were said: they deserve that it be said to them «eat and enjoy yourselves», then (they are described) by their being criminals and by their being such that when it is said to them «pray», they do not pray. إذا is a future adverb containing the sense of condition; the clause قيل is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; لهم is attached to قيل; the clause اركعوا is the speech of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); and the clause لا يركعون has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ) Its parsing has preceded. (فَبِأَيِّ حَدِيثٍ بَعْدَهُ يُؤْمِنُونَ) The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (fāʾ that discloses an omitted condition), i.e. if they do not believe in the Qurʾān, then in what thing will they believe? بأي is attached to يؤمنون; حديث is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation); بعده is an adverb attached to an omitted adjective of حديث; and يؤمنون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying: «إن المتقين في ظلال وعيون وفواكه مما يشتهون» there is a majāz mursal (metonymic trope) whose relation is locality (al-maḥalliyya), namely Paradise, because the shades extend, the springs flow and the fruits ripen in it.
2- And in His saying: «وإذا قيل لهم اركعوا» there is also a majāz mursal, whose relation is part-for-whole (al-baʿḍiyya), because He named the prayer by the name of one of its parts, namely bowing (al-rukūʿ). He singled out bowing for mention, although the prayer includes many actions, only because the Arabs used to disdain bowing and prostrating. Muqātil said: it was revealed about Thaqīf; they said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: relieve us of the prayer, for we do not bend down; it is a disgrace. He refused and said: there is no good in a religion that has no prayer in it — and in a narration: no bowing in it and no prostration.

* Benefits:
The grammarians said: in the like of «ما تأتينا فتحدّثنا» both the accusative and the nominative are permissible in the second verb. The accusative is from two aspects that share the feature that the second differs from the first: one of the two meanings is «you do not come to us talking», and the other aspect is «you do not come to us, so how could you talk to us?». As for the nominative, it is on two aspects. One is that the verb is a partner of the first, entering with it into the negation, as if you said «you do not come to us and you do not talk to us», so they are two negated clauses. The second aspect is that the meaning of ما تأتينا فتحدّثنا is «you do not come to us, yet you talk to us». The Exalted said: هذا يوم لا ينطقون ولا يؤذن لهم فيعتذرون, i.e. so they do not make excuses. And from it is the saying of Jamīl ibn Maʿmar al-ʿUdhrī:
ألم تسأل الربع القواء فينطق ... وهل يخبرنك اليوم بيداء سملق
(Did you not ask the deserted encampment — and it speaks? Yet would a barren, level waste tell you anything today?)
He cut off ينطق from what precedes it and made it nominative as a resumption, i.e. it speaks in any case. Sībawayh said: «He did not make the first the cause of the second, but he made it speak in any case.»

farraa:1-1.t:
[120/b] His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلْمُرْسَلاَتِ عُرْفاً﴾.
It is said: they are the angels. As for His saying (عرفا): it is said: they were sent with what is right (المعروف); and it is said: they followed one another like the mane (عرف) of a horse. The Arabs say: تركتُ الناس إلى فلان عُرفاً واحداً (I left the people [going] to So-and-so in one continuous line), when they head towards him in great numbers.

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱلْعَاصِفَاتِ عَصْفاً﴾.
They are the winds.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وٱلنَّاشِرَاتِ نَشْراً﴾.
They are the winds that bring rain.

farraa:4-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱلْفَارِقَاتِ فَرْقاً﴾.
They are the angels, who descend with the distinguishing (الفرق) — with the revelation [that distinguishes] between the lawful and the unlawful, and with its detailed exposition; and they are also:
﴿فَٱلْمُلْقِيَاتِ ذِكْراً﴾.
They are the angels who deliver the Reminder to the prophets.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿عُذْراً أَوْ نُذْراً﴾.
Al-Aʿmash read it lightened (without vowel on the dhāl), and ʿĀṣim made (النُّذر) alone heavy (with ḍamma on the dhāl). The people of the Hijaz and al-Ḥasan make both عذراً and نذراً heavy. It is a maṣdar (verbal noun), whether lightened or heavy. عذراً أو نذراً are accusative, meaning: they were sent with what they were sent with as an excuse-giving (iʿdhār) from Allah and a warning (indhār).

farraa:8-8.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِذَا ٱلنُّجُومُ طُمِسَتْ﴾.
Their light is gone.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلرُّسُلُ أُقِّتَتْ﴾.
The readers agree on reading it with hamza. In the reading of ʿAbdullāh it is: "وقِّتت" with wāw, and Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī read it: "وُقِتتْ" with wāw, lightened. It took a hamza only because when wāw is the first letter and carries a ḍamma it is turned into hamza; of that kind is your saying: صلّى القوم أُحداناً (the people prayed one by one) [from وُحدان]. Someone recited to me:
يَحل أحِيدهُ، ويُقالُ: بَعْلٌ * ومِثلُ تَموُّلٍ منهُ افتقارُ
(His being single [أحيد, from وحيد] becomes lawful [i.e. ends], and it is said: a husband; and like getting rich, from it comes poverty.)
And they say: هذه أجوهٌ حسان (these are handsome faces) with hamza [for وجوه]. That is because the ḍamma on wāw is heavy, just as the kasra on yāʾ was heavy.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أُقِّتَتْ﴾: they were gathered for their appointed time on the Day of Resurrection [121/a].

farraa:12-13.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لأَيِّ يَوْمٍ أُجِّلَتْ﴾.
He makes the servants wonder at that day, then He said: ﴿لِيَوْمِ ٱلْفَصْلِ﴾.

farraa:16-17.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلَمْ نُهْلِكِ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ﴾ ﴿ثُمَّ نُتْبِعُهُمُ ٱلآخِرِينَ﴾.
With the nominative. In the reading of ʿAbdullāh it is: "ألم نهلك الأولين وسنتبعهم الآخرين", and this is evidence that it is resumptive (mustaʾnafa), not coordinated back onto (نهلك). If you put it in the jussive, on [the sense]: "Did We not decree the destruction of the former ones and making the later ones follow them", it would be a good interpretation with the jussive; because decreeing applies to both the past and the future.

farraa:23-23.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَقَدَرْنَا فَنِعْمَ ٱلْقَادِرُونَ﴾.
It is mentioned of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah have mercy on him, and of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī that they read it with shadda (فقدّرنا), while al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim read it lightened. Do not consider it unlikely that the meaning with shadda and without it is the same; because the Arabs say: قُدِّر عليه الموتُ (death was decreed for him), and قُدِّر عليه رزقه (his provision was straitened for him), and قُدِر عليه, with the lightened and the doubled form. Those who read it lightened argued, saying: if it were so, it would have been: فنعم المقدِّرون. But the Arabs sometimes combine the two forms; Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَمَهِّلِ الْكَافِرِينَ أَمْهِلْهُمْ رُوَيْداً﴾. And al-Aʿshā said:
وأنْكرتْنى، وما كان الَّذى نَكِرتْ * من الحوادثِ إلاَّ الشيبَ والصَّلَعا
(She disowned me — and what she disowned of the events was nothing but grey hair and baldness.)

farraa:25-26.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ ٱلأَرْضَ كِفَاتاً﴾ ﴿أَحْيَآءً وَأَمْواتاً﴾.
It holds them (تكفتهم) alive on its surface, in their houses and dwellings, and holds them dead in its belly, i.e. it keeps them and guards them. Your putting الأحياء and الأموات in the accusative is because الكفات acts upon them, as though you said: Did We not make the earth a holder of the living and the dead (كفاتَ أحياءٍ وأمواتٍ); so when you add tanwīn, you put [what follows] in the accusative — just as whoever reads it reads: ﴿أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ فِى يَوْمٍ ذِى مَسْغَبَةٍ، يَتِيماً﴾, and as one reads: ﴿فَجَزَاءٌ مِثْلَ ما قتل﴾; and similar to it: ﴿فِدْيَةٌ طعامَ مِسْكِينٍ﴾ [121/b].

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِلَىٰ ظِلٍّ ذِي ثَلاَثِ شُعَبٍ﴾.
It is said that a tongue comes out of the Fire and surrounds them like a pavilion; then three branches of smoke branch off from it and shade them, until their reckoning is finished [and they go] to the Fire.

farraa:32-32.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَٱلْقَصْرِ﴾ — He means the قصر (castle), one of the castles at the watering places of the Arabs. Its singular and its plural are both [good] Arabic; Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: ﴿سَيُهْزَمُ الْجَمْعُ ويُوَلُّون الدُّبَر﴾, its meaning being: الأدبار (the backs). It is as though the Qur'an came down according to what the Arabs like, namely the agreement of the verse-endings. Do you not see that He said: ﴿إِلَى شَىْءٍ نُّكُرٍ﴾, making it heavy (with ḍamma on the kāf) in (اقتربت) because its verses are heavy, while He said: ﴿فَحاسَبْنَاهَا حِسَاباً شَدِيداً وعذَّبناها عَذاباً نُّكْراً﴾? The readers agreed on making the first heavy and this one light. Similar to it is: ﴿الشَّمْسُ والْقَمَرُ بحُسْبَانٍ﴾, while He said: ﴿جَزَاءً مِّنْ رَبِّكَ عَطاءً حِساباً﴾. So the verse-endings were made to run along these courses; and that is more than a book can comprehend, but this much of it suffices you, if Allah wills.
It is also said: كالقَصَر, like the stumps of palm trees; but I do not favour that, because it is among lightened verses, and besides, it is the camel that is compared to the castle. Do you not see His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿كَأَنَّهُ جِمالاتٌ صُفْر﴾? الصُّفر are the black camels: you do not see any black camel without it being tinged with yellow; that is why the Arabs called black camels صُفر (yellow), just as they called gazelles أُدْم (tawny/dark) because of the darkness that overlies their whiteness. The readers differed over "جمالات": ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd and his companions read: "جمالةٌ".
He said: [Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl narrated to me from ʿAṭāʾ from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, tracing it back to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah have mercy on him), that he read: "جِمالاتٌ". That is the preferable of the two to me, because جِمال is more common than جِمالة in the speech of the Arabs. It [جمالة] is permissible, as one says حجر and حجارة, and ذَكَر and ذِكارة, except that the first is more common. If you say جِمالات, its singular is جِمال, just as they said رجال and رجالات, and بيوت and بيوتات. It may also be that you make the singular of جمالات be جمالة. [It has been reported from one of the readers: جُمالات]; this may be from a thing that is gathered (المُجمَل), or جُمالات may be a plural formed from a plural, of الجمال, as they said: الرَّخِل, and الرُّخال and الرِّخال.

farraa:35-35.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هَـٰذَا يَوْمُ لاَ يَنطِقُونَ﴾.
The readers agreed on the nominative for اليوم. If it were put in the accusative, it would be permissible on two grounds. One of them: when the Arabs annex اليوم and الليلة to a فعل or يفعل [verb], or to a whole statement in which there is no genitive, they put اليوم in the accusative [even] in the position of the genitive and the nominative; that is one ground. The other: that you take this as meaning a whole action [summarised] from "لا ينطقون" — Allah's threat and His reward — as though you said: this affair is on the day they do not speak. The first ground is better, and the nominative is more common in the speech of the Arabs. The meaning of His saying "This is a day on which they do not speak" and do not excuse themselves is: at certain hours of that day. That is clear in this kind [of expression]. You say in speech: آتيك يوم يقدُم أبوك (I will come to you on the day your father arrives), and يوم تقدَم (on the day you arrive), the meaning being: at the hour he arrives, not the whole day. If it meant the whole day, it would not be permissible in speech to annex it to a فعل, nor to a يفعل, nor to a whole statement, as in your saying: أتيتك حين الحجاجُ أميرٌ (I came to you when al-Ḥajjāj was governor).
The Arabs only allowed: أتيتك يوم مات فلان (I came to you on the day So-and-so died) and آتيك يوم يقدم فلان (I will come to you on the day So-and-so arrives), because they mean: I came to you when (إذ) he arrived, and when (إذا) he arrives; and إذ and إذا do not seek nouns, they only seek the verb. Since اليوم and الليلة and all [expressions of] times carry their meaning, they were annexed to فعل and يفعل and to a noun about which something is predicated, as the poet said: [122/b]
أزمان من يرد الصنيعة يصطنع * مِننًا، ومن يرد الزهادة يزهد
(In the times when whoever wished to do favours would do favours, and whoever wished for abstinence would abstain.)

farraa:36-36.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ يُؤْذَنُ لَهُمْ فَيَعْتَذِرُونَ﴾.
With the fāʾ you intend it to be coordinated (nasaq) with what precedes it. That was chosen because the verses [end] in nūn; had it been said فيعتذروا, it would not agree with the verses. Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿لاَ يُقْضَى عَلَيْهِمْ فَيَمُوتُوا﴾ with the accusative, and both are correct. Similar to it: ﴿مَنْ ذَا الَّذِى يُقْرِضُ اللهَ قَرْضاً حَسَناً فَيُضَاعِفهُ﴾ and (فيضاعفَه). He said: Abū ʿAbdullāh said: that is how al-Kisāʾī, al-Farrāʾ and Ḥamza used to read: (فيضاعفُه).

farraa:39-39.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَإِن كَانَ لَكمُ كَيْدٌ فَكِيدُونِ﴾.
If you have any stratagem, then use it for yourselves.

farraa:48-48.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿وَإذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱرْكَعُواْ لاَ يَرْكَعُونَ﴾.
He says: when they are commanded to pray, they do not pray.

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: The second clause «انطلقوا» is a badal (substitute) of the first; «ذي»: naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: His saying «لا ظليل»: «لا» is negating; «ظليل»: naʿt (adjective) of {ظِلٍّ}; the clause «ولا يغني» is conjoined to the single word «ظليل».

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: The clause «إنها ترمي» is resumptive; «كالقصر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «لشرر».

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: The clause «كأنه جمالة» is a second naʿt (adjective) of «لشرر».

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: «يوم»: khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ); the clause «لا ينطقون» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: The clause «فيعتذرون» is conjoined to the clause «لا يؤذن لهم».

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: The clause «هذا يوم الفصل» is resumptive, and the clause «جمعناكم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «يوم الفصل», the link being implied (muqaddar), i.e.: فيه (in it); «الأولين» is a noun conjoined to the kāf in «جمعناكم».

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: The clause «فإن كان لكم كيد» is conjoined to the clause {هَذَا يَوْمُ}; and his saying «فكيدون»: the fāʾ is the linking one, and it is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the nūn is that of protection (wiqāya), and the implied yāʾ has been omitted.

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: His saying «وفواكه»: a noun conjoined to «عيون», genitive (majrūr) with fatḥa because it is a diptote; the preposition «مما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «فواكه».

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: The clause «كلوا» is maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech) of an implied saying, and the implied saying is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in the adverb, i.e.: being in shades, that being said to them; «هنيئا»: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the preposition «بما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «هنيئا».

harrat-mujtaba:44-44.t: The clause «نجزي» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن», and the kāf is nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq (substitute for the absolute object), i.e.: We recompense them with a recompense like that recompense.

harrat-mujtaba:46-46.t: The clause «كلوا» is resumptive; «قليلا»: nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq (substitute for the absolute object), i.e.: a little eating; and the clause «إنكم مجرمون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:48-48.t: (وإذا قيل لهم اركعوا لا يركعون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The conditional clause is resumptive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of «قيل» is the pronoun of the maṣdar (verbal noun).

harrat-mujtaba:50-50.t: The clause «يؤمنون» is resumptive, and the preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the adverb «بعده» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of "حديث.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: (والمرسلات عرفا) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) «أقسم» (I swear); «عرفا» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e.: in succession.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: «عصفا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) emphasising the active participle; his words «فالعاصفات»: a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «المرسلات».

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: (والناشرات نشرا) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] A noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «العاصفات»; «نَشْرًا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: «ذكرا» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: (إنما توعدون لواقع) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is the answer to the oath; «إن» is abrogating (nāsikha); «ما» is its noun and «واقع» its khabar (predicate); and the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa).

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The fāʾ is resumptive; «النجوم» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of an omitted verb explained by what follows it; the clause «طمست» is explicative; and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e.: what you are promised will occur.

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: (لأي يوم أجلت) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The preposition phrase is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أجِّلت»; the clause «أجِّلت» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) of a concealed saying, i.e.: it will be said; this concealed saying is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nominative of {أُقِّتَتْ}, i.e.: it being said about them.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The preposition phrase «ليوم» is a badal (substitute) from {لأَيِّ يَوْمٍ}, with the preposition repeated.

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The wāw is resumptive; «ما» is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); and the clause «ما يوم» is in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb «أدراك», which is suspended.

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: «ويل» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); what permitted beginning with it is that it is an imprecation; «يومئذ» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «ويل»; the preposition phrase «للمكذبين» is attached to the khabar (predicate); and the clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: (ألم نهلك الأولين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: (كذلك نفعل بالمجرمين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The kāf is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and the clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The clause «فجعلناه» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {نَخْلُقْكُمْ}; the preposition phrase «في قرار» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جعل».

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The preposition phrase «إلى قدر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «جعلناه».

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The clause «فقدرنا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «جعلناه»; the clause «فنعم القادرون» is resumptive, and the one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) is omitted, i.e.: We (نحن).

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: «أحياء» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the maṣdar (verbal noun) {كِفَاتًا}, i.e.: it holds the living and the dead, meaning it gathers them, living on its back and dead in its belly.

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: The preposition phrase «فيها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted second object, and «ماء» is a second object.

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: The clause «انطلقوا» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied (muqaddar) saying.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted: (عرفا): accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (المرسلات), which are the winds sent one after another. Whoever makes (المرسلات) the angels makes (عرفا) accusative on the basis of omitting the preposition, i.e. "Allah sends them with (العرف)", i.e. with what is right (المعروف).

mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying (عصفا) and (نشرا): two emphatic maṣdars (verbal nouns).

mekki-muskil:5-5.t: His saying (ذكرا): a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

mekki-muskil:6-6.t: His saying (عذرا أو نذرا): accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun). Whoever reads the dhāl with ḍamma makes it the plural of (عذير) and (نذير), in the sense of "excusing" and "warning". Whoever makes the dhāl vowelless, it may be lightened from the ḍamma form, in the sense of "excusing" and "warning", as He said (فكيف كان نكير), i.e. "My disapproval of them", i.e. the outcome of that. It may also be not lightened, its vowellessness being original, as a maṣdar on the pattern of (شكر).

mekki-muskil:7-7.t:
His saying (إنما توعدون لواقع): (ما) is the noun of (إن) and (لواقع) is the khabar (predicate). The hāʾ is omitted from (توعدون), and with it the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما) is completed; its implied form is (توعدونه). Its omission from the ṣila is good because of the length of the noun; close to it is its omission from an adjective; and its omission from a khabar is not permissible except in poetry. (إن) [with its clause] is the answer to the preceding oath.
His saying (فإذا النجوم طمست): (النجوم) is, according to the Basrans, nominative by an implied verb, because (إذا) carries the meaning of a conditional, so it is more fitting with the verb. Its like is (إذا الشمس كورت), (إذا السماء انشقت) and (إذا السماء انفطرت), and it is frequent in the Qur'an. The Kufans said: what follows (إذا) is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what comes after it is the khabar. The answer of (إذا) in His saying, the Exalted (فإذا النجوم) is omitted, its implied form being "the decision will take place". It is also said that its answer is (ويل يومئذ للمكذبين).

mekki-muskil:13-13.t: His saying (ليوم الفصل): the lām is attached to an implied verb, its implied form being "they were deferred for the Day of Decision". It is also said that it is a badal (substitute) from (أي) [Translator's note: i.e. from (لأي يوم)] with the preposition repeated. It is also said that the lām means (إلى) "until".

mekki-muskil:14-14.t: His saying (وما أدراك ما يوم الفصل): it was mentioned before, in al-Ḥāqqa and elsewhere.

mekki-muskil:15-15.t: His saying (ويل يومئذ للمكذبين): (ويل), wherever it occurs in this sūra and what resembles it, is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (يومئذ) is an adverbial governed by the meaning of (ويل), and (للمكذبين) is the khabar (predicate).

mekki-muskil:25-25.t:
His saying (كفاتا): the second object of (نجعل), because it means "We make into" (نصير).
His saying (أحياء وأمواتا): two ḥāls (circumstantials), i.e. the earth gathers them in these two states; (الكفت) is gathering. It is also said that it is accusative governed by (كفات), i.e. it gathers the living and the dead, i.e. it holds them, living on its surface and dead in its interior.

mekki-muskil:35-35.t: His saying (هذا يوم لا ينطقون): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), the reference being to the day. Al-Aʿmash and others read (يوم) with fatḥa; so it may be indeclinable (mabnī) according to the Kufans because it is annexed to the verb, while being nominative in meaning. It may also be in the position of the accusative, the reference being to something other than the day. And the fatḥa may be an inflection [of the accusative], which is the school of the Basrans, because the verb is declinable, and according to the Basrans it is made indeclinable only when annexed to an indeclinable word; so the reference is to something other than the day, and it is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ in every case.

mekki-muskil:44-44.t:
His saying (كذلك نجزي): the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a recompense like that We recompense".
His saying (وتمتعوا قليلا): (قليلا) is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar [Translator's note: printed «لصدر»] or of an omitted adverbial, its implied form being "and enjoy a little enjoyment" or "for a little time". It is accusative by (تمتعوا) in both aspects, except that once it is a mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial) and once a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿والمرسلات﴾: the wāw is a particle of oath and genitive, and «المرسلات» is a noun in the genitive by the wāw of oath, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear" (أُقسم).
﴿عرفا﴾: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «المرسلات», accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, i.e. "in succession"; or standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "by those sent forth, a sending"; or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative, «العرف» meaning «المعروف» (kindness), i.e. "they were sent for beneficence and kindness"; and it was said that ﴿عرفا﴾ is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "with kindness" (بالعرف). The oath clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿فالعاصفات﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction for immediate succession, and «العاصفات» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to ﴿المرسلات﴾, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.
﴿عصفا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿والناشرات﴾: the wāw is a particle of genitive and oath, and «الناشرات» is a noun in the genitive by the wāw of oath, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear" (أُقسم). Or: the wāw is a conjunction, and «الناشرات» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «العاصفات», genitive by the kasra.
﴿نشرا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa; if the wāw in ﴿والناشرات﴾ is taken as the wāw of oath, the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿فالفارقات﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction for immediate succession, and «الفارقات» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to ﴿الناشرات﴾, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.
﴿فرقا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿فالملقيات﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction for immediate succession, and «الملقيات» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to ﴿الفارقات﴾, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.
﴿ذكرا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿الملقيات﴾, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿عذرا﴾: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa; or a badal (substitute) from ﴿ذكرا﴾; or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿الملقيات﴾, i.e. "excusing" or "warning".
﴿أو﴾: a conjunction.
﴿نذرا﴾: maʿṭūf (conjoined) to ﴿عذرا﴾, accusative by the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿إنما﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, with no grammatical position; and «ما» is a relative noun indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb), the noun of «إن».
﴿توعدون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, because it is one of the five verbs; it is passive (built for that whose agent is not named); the wāw of the plural is a pronoun indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of a nominative, nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, i.e. "that which you are promised" (إن الذي توعدونه); the clause «توعدون» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿لواقع﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and «واقع» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن», nominative by the ḍamma; the clause has no grammatical position, because it is the answer to the oath.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿فإذا﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and «إذا» is an adverb (ẓarf) for future time, containing the meaning of condition, governing its protasis in the genitive and itself made accusative by its apodosis.
﴿النجوم﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma, of an omitted verb indicated by the verb mentioned after it, its implied form being "طُمسَت" (were obliterated). The clause made up of the omitted verb and the nāʾib fāʿil is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it.
