﴿طمست﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; it is passive (built for that whose agent is not named); the nāʾib fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "hiya" (they); the clause ﴿طمست﴾ is explicative (tafsīriyya), with no grammatical position; and the clause ﴿فإذا النجوم طمست﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿وإذا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «إذا» is an adverb (ẓarf) for future time, containing the meaning of condition, governing its protasis in the genitive and itself made accusative by its apodosis.
﴿السماء﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma, of an omitted verb indicated by the verb mentioned after it, its implied form being "فُرجت" (was split open). The clause made up of the omitted verb and the nāʾib fāʿil is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it.
﴿فرجت﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; it is passive (built for that whose agent is not named); the nāʾib fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "hiya" (it); the clause ﴿فرجت﴾ is explicative (tafsīriyya), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿وإذا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «إذا» is an adverb (ẓarf) for future time, containing the meaning of condition, governing its protasis in the genitive and itself made accusative by its apodosis.
﴿الجبال﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma, of an omitted verb indicated by the verb mentioned after it, its implied form being "نُسفت" (were blown away). The clause made up of the omitted verb and the nāʾib fāʿil is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it.
﴿نسفت﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; it is passive (built for that whose agent is not named); the nāʾib fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "hiya" (they); the clause ﴿نسفت﴾ is explicative (tafsīriyya), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿وإذا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «إذا» is an adverb (ẓarf) for future time, containing the meaning of condition, governing its protasis in the genitive and itself made accusative by its apodosis.
﴿الرسل﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma, of an omitted verb indicated by the verb mentioned after it, its implied form being "أقتت" (were given their appointed time). The clause made up of the omitted verb and the nāʾib fāʿil is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it.
﴿أقتت﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; it is passive (built for that whose agent is not named); the nāʾib fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "hiya" (they); the clause ﴿أقتت﴾ is explicative (tafsīriyya), with no grammatical position.
The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being: "what you are promised will occur"; or the apodosis is ﴿لأي يوم أجلت﴾ by implying a saying, i.e. ﴿يقال لأي يوم أجلت﴾ ("it will be said: for what day were they deferred?"), so that the verb [of saying] is in reality the apodosis.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿لأي﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أجلت﴾; «أيّ» is muḍāf.
﴿يوم﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.
﴿أجلت﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; it is passive (built for that whose agent is not named); the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "hiya" (they); the clause is the content of an omitted saying, in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in ﴿أقتت﴾, i.e. "it is said: for what day were they deferred?"; or it has no grammatical position if it is made the apodosis of «إذا».

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿ليوم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being ﴿أُجِّلت﴾, i.e. "they were deferred to the Day of Decision"; or a badal (substitute) from ﴿لأي يوم﴾; «يوم» is muḍāf.
﴿الفصل﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and «ما» is an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ), mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿أدراك﴾: a past verb indeclinable on a fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa" (it), referring back to ﴿ما﴾; the kāf is the pronoun of the one addressed, indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb), first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿أدراك﴾ is in the position of a nominative, the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ ﴿ما﴾.
﴿ما﴾: an interrogative noun, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ.
﴿يوم﴾: the khabar of the second ﴿ما﴾, nominative by the ḍamma.
﴿الفصل﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra; the clause ﴿ما يوم الفصل﴾, made up of the mubtadaʾ and khabar, is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the second and third objects of ﴿أدراك﴾; and the clause ﴿وما أدراك ...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿ويل﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿يومئذ﴾: «يوم» is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ويل﴾ or to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿ويل﴾; «يوم» is muḍāf; and «إذٍ» is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on a sukūn implied (muqaddar) because its place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of a genitive (majrūr), muḍāf ilayhi; the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, the implied form being: "on the day when [judgement] is passed between the creatures".
﴿للمكذبين﴾: the lām is a preposition, and «المكذبين» is a noun in the genitive by the lām, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ, because it is a sound masculine plural; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of ﴿ويل﴾; and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿ألم﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (al-istifhām al-taqrīrī), and «لم» is a particle of negation, conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning], and jussive.
﴿نهلك﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾, the sign of its jussive being the sukūn, the kāf being given a kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being ﴿نحن﴾ (We).
﴿الأولين﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ, because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction for sequence with delay, or resumptive.
﴿نتبعهم﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "naḥnu" (We); the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of an accusative, first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the mīm is the sign of the plural.
﴿الآخرين﴾: second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ, because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is conjoined to the clause ﴿ألم نهلك...﴾, or resumptive, and on both views it has no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿كذلك﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "like that doing We do".
﴿نفعل﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being ﴿نحن﴾ (We).
﴿بالمجرمين﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition, and «المجرمين» is a noun in the genitive by the bāʾ, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ, because it is a sound masculine plural; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿نفعل﴾; and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿ويل﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿يومئذ﴾: «يوم» is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ويل﴾ or to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿ويل﴾; «يوم» is muḍāf; and «إذٍ» is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on a sukūn implied (muqaddar) because its place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of a genitive (majrūr), muḍāf ilayhi; the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, the implied form being: "on the day when [judgement] is passed between the creatures".
﴿للمكذبين﴾: the lām is a preposition, and «المكذبين» is a noun in the genitive by the lām, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ, because it is a sound masculine plural; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of ﴿ويل﴾; and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿ألم﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (al-istifhām al-taqrīrī), and «لم» is a particle of negation, conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning], and jussive.
﴿نخلقكم﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾, the sign of its jussive being the sukūn; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "naḥnu" (We); the kāf is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the mīm is the sign of the plural.
﴿من ماء﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نخلقكم﴾.
﴿مهين﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ماء﴾, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿فجعلناه﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «جعلناه» is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn; ﴿نا﴾ is a pronoun indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of a nominative, fāʿil (agent); and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of an accusative, first mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿في قرار﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second mafʿūl bihi of ﴿جعلناه﴾.
﴿مكين﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿قرار﴾, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra; the clause has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the one before it.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿إلى قدر﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "deferred to a known term".
﴿معلوم﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿قدر﴾, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿فقدرنا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «قدرنا» is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn; ﴿نا﴾ is a pronoun indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of a nominative, fāʿil (agent).
﴿فنعم﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «نعم» is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing praise.
﴿القادرون﴾: fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw, because it is a sound masculine plural; the one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bil-madḥ) is omitted, i.e. "We".

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿ويل﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿يومئذ﴾: «يوم» is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ويل﴾ or to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿ويل﴾; «يوم» is muḍāf; and «إذٍ» is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on a sukūn implied (muqaddar) because its place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of a genitive (majrūr), muḍāf ilayhi; the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, the implied form being: "on the day when [judgement] is passed between the creatures".
﴿للمكذبين﴾: the lām is a preposition, and «المكذبين» is a noun in the genitive by the lām, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ, because it is a sound masculine plural; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of ﴿ويل﴾; and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t:
﴿ألم﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (al-istifhām al-taqrīrī), and «لم» is a particle of negation, conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning], and jussive.
﴿نجعل﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being ﴿نحن﴾ (We).
﴿الأرض﴾: first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿نجعل﴾, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.
﴿كفاتا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi of ﴿نجعل﴾, accusative by the fatḥa; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:26-26.t: ﴿أحياء وأمواتا﴾: both are accusative (manṣūb) as objects (mafʿūl bihi) of ﴿كفاتًا﴾, if it is established that «كفاتًا» is a maṣdar (verbal noun), or the plural of «كافت», since that is an active participle; but if it is not a maṣdar but rather a noun of place, then they are made accusative by an implied verb indicated by ﴿كفاتًا﴾, its implied form being "it draws together" (تكفت), the meaning being: it draws [people] together living upon its back and dead within its belly; or the meaning is: "it draws you together, living and dead", so that they are both accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun.

muyesser-irab:27-27.t:
﴿وجعلنا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «جعلنا» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent).
﴿فيها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿جعلنا﴾ if it has the meaning of "We created", and in the position of the second object if «جعلنا» has the meaning of "We made [it] become".
﴿رواسي﴾: the object of ﴿جعلنا﴾.
﴿شامخات﴾: an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿رواسي﴾.
﴿وأسقيناكم﴾: conjoined to ﴿جعلنا﴾.
﴿ماء﴾: second mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿فراتًا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ماء﴾.

muyesser-irab:28-28.t:
﴿ويل﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿يومئذ﴾: «يوم» is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ويل﴾ or to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿ويل﴾; «يوم» is muḍāf; and «إذٍ» is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on a sukūn implied (muqaddar) because its place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of a genitive (majrūr), muḍāf ilayhi; the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, the implied form being: "on the day when [judgement] is passed between the creatures".
﴿للمكذبين﴾: the lām is a preposition, and «المكذبين» is a noun in the genitive by the lām, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ, because it is a sound masculine plural; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of ﴿ويل﴾; and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t:
﴿انطلقوا﴾: the clause is the content of an omitted saying, the implied form being: "it will be said to them: proceed"; «انطلقوا» is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the elision of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿إلى ما﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿انطلقوا﴾.
﴿كنتم﴾: «كان» is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the tāʾ is its noun; the clause «كنتم» is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿به﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تكذبون﴾.
﴿تكذبون﴾: an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause «تكذبون» is the khabar of ﴿كنتم﴾, and the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is the pronoun in «به»; the clause of the omitted saying is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:30-30.t:
﴿انطلقوا﴾: a tawkīd (emphasis) of the first ﴿انطلقوا﴾.
﴿إلى ظل﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿انطلقوا﴾.
﴿ذي﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ظل﴾, genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ, because it is one of the five nouns.
﴿ثلاث﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿شعب﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:31-31.t:
﴿لا﴾: negating.
﴿ظليل﴾: a negated naʿt (adjective).
﴿ولا يغني﴾: conjoined to the negated [adjective]; «يغني» is an imperfect verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is "huwa" (it), the shade.
﴿من اللهب﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يغني﴾ [Translator's note: in the source the closing bracket falls after «يغن», leaving the yāʾ outside it]; the clause is in the position of a genitive, i.e. "not availing them anything against the heat of the flame".

muyesser-irab:32-32.t:
﴿إنها﴾: the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya); «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿ها﴾ is its noun, the pronoun referring back to ﴿جهنم﴾.
﴿ترمي﴾: an imperfect verb, and the yāʾ is the fāʿil (agent) [Translator's note: so in the source; the fāʿil of «ترمي» is in fact a latent pronoun "hiya" (it), the yāʾ being part of the verb's root]; the clause «ترمي» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن».
﴿بشرر﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ترمي﴾.
﴿كالقصر﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning «مثل» (like), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of a genitive, a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿شرر﴾; and ﴿القصر﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:33-33.t:
﴿كأنه﴾: the clause is a second naʿt (adjective) of ﴿شرر﴾; «كأن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is its noun.
﴿جمالة﴾: the khabar (predicate) of «كأن».
﴿صفر﴾: a naʿt of ﴿جمالة﴾.

muyesser-irab:34-34.t:
﴿ويل﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿يومئذ﴾: «يوم» is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ويل﴾ or to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿ويل﴾; «يوم» is muḍāf; and «إذٍ» is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on a sukūn implied (muqaddar) because its place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of a genitive (majrūr), muḍāf ilayhi; the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, the implied form being: "on the day when [judgement] is passed between the creatures".
﴿للمكذبين﴾: the lām is a preposition, and «المكذبين» is a noun in the genitive by the lām, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ, because it is a sound masculine plural; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of ﴿ويل﴾; and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:35-35.t:
﴿هذا﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; «هذا» is mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿يوم﴾: its khabar (predicate).
﴿لا﴾: negating.
﴿ينطقون﴾: an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause «لا ينطقون» is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it.

muyesser-irab:36-36.t:
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «لا» is negating.
﴿يؤذن﴾: an imperfect verb, passive (built for that whose agent is not named); the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa" (it).
﴿لهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يؤذن﴾.
﴿فيعتذرون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «يعتذرون» is an imperfect verb conjoined to ﴿يؤذن﴾.

muyesser-irab:37-37.t:
﴿ويل﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿يومئذ﴾: «يوم» is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ويل﴾ or to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿ويل﴾; «يوم» is muḍāf; and «إذٍ» is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on a sukūn implied (muqaddar) because its place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of a genitive (majrūr), muḍāf ilayhi; the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, the implied form being: "on the day when [judgement] is passed between the creatures".

muyesser-irab:38-38.t:
﴿هذا﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; «هذا» is mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿يوم﴾: its khabar (predicate).
﴿الفصل﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿جمعناكم﴾: a past verb; ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil (agent) and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿والأولين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, or for accompaniment (maʿiyya); and «الأولين» is conjoined to the kāf, or a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment).

muyesser-irab:39-39.t:
﴿فإن﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «إن» is conditional.
﴿كان﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb.
﴿لكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar of kāna.
﴿كيد﴾: its postponed noun.
﴿فكيدون﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis of the conditional, because it is a request clause (jumla ṭalabiyya); «كيدون» is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the elision of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), the nūn is for protection (al-wiqāya), and the elided yāʾ of the speaker is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:40-40.t:
﴿ويل﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿يومئذ﴾: «يوم» is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ويل﴾ or to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿ويل﴾; «يوم» is muḍāf; and «إذٍ» is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on a sukūn implied (muqaddar) because its place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of a genitive (majrūr), muḍāf ilayhi; the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, the implied form being: "on the day when [judgement] is passed between the creatures".

muyesser-irab:41-41.t:
﴿إن المتقين﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and «المتقين» is its noun.
﴿في ظلال﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of «إن».
﴿وعيون﴾: conjoined to ﴿ظلال﴾.

muyesser-irab:42-42.t:

﴿مما﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿فواكه﴾.
﴿يشتهون﴾: an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿يشتهون﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.

muyesser-irab:43-43.t:
﴿كلوا﴾: an imperative verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿واشربوا﴾: conjoined to ﴿كلوا﴾; the clause is the content of an omitted saying, and this content is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of «المتقين» in the adverbial expression that is in ﴿ظلال﴾, i.e. "they are settled in shades, this being said to them".
﴿هنيئًا﴾: an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a wholesome eating"; or a ḥāl, i.e. "enjoying wholesomely".
﴿بما﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿هنيئا﴾; the bāʾ is causal (sababiyya), and «ما» is a relative.
﴿كنتم﴾: the clause «كنتم» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. «كان» is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, the tāʾ is its noun, and the clause «تعملون» is its khabar.

muyesser-irab:44-44.t:
﴿إنا﴾: ﴿إنّ﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun.
﴿كذلك﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning «مثل» (like), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb), an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun) placed before its governor, i.e. "a recompense like that We give the doers of good"; and «ذلك»: ﴿ذا﴾ is a demonstrative in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi, the lām is for distance, and the kāf is a particle of address.
﴿نجزي﴾: an imperfect verb; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "naḥnu" (We).
﴿المحسنين﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿نجزي المحسنين﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of ﴿إنّ﴾.

﴿يومئذ﴾: «يوم» is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ويل﴾ or to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿ويل﴾; «يوم» is muḍāf; and «إذٍ» is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on a sukūn implied (muqaddar) because its place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of a genitive (majrūr), muḍāf ilayhi; the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, the implied form being: "on the day when [judgement] is passed between the creatures".

muyesser-irab:46-46.t:
﴿كلوا﴾: an imperative verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿وتمتعوا﴾: conjoined to ﴿كلوا﴾.
﴿قليلًا﴾: accusative (manṣūb) as an adverb of time.
﴿إنكم﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿كم﴾ is its noun.
﴿مجرمون﴾: the khabar (predicate) of «إن»; the clause «إنكم مجرمون» is causal (taʿlīliyya).

muyesser-irab:47-47.t:
﴿ويل﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿يومئذ﴾: «يوم» is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ويل﴾ or to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿ويل﴾; «يوم» is muḍāf; and «إذٍ» is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on a sukūn implied (muqaddar) because its place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of a genitive (majrūr), muḍāf ilayhi; the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, the implied form being: "on the day when [judgement] is passed between the creatures".

muyesser-irab:48-48.t:
﴿وإذا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «إذا» is an adverb (ẓarf) containing the meaning of condition.
﴿قيل﴾: an indeclinable (mabnī) past verb; the clause ﴿قيل﴾ is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it.
﴿لهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قيل﴾.
﴿اركعوا﴾: an imperative verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿اركعوا﴾ is the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿لا﴾: negating.
﴿يركعون﴾: an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause ﴿لا يركعون﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.

muyesser-irab:49-49.t:
﴿ويل﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿يومئذ﴾: «يوم» is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ويل﴾ or to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿ويل﴾; «يوم» is muḍāf; and «إذٍ» is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on a sukūn implied (muqaddar) because its place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of a genitive (majrūr), muḍāf ilayhi; the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, the implied form being: "on the day when [judgement] is passed between the creatures".

muyesser-irab:50-50.t:
﴿فبأي﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), and «بأي» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يؤمنون﴾.
﴿حديث﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿بعده﴾: an adverb (ẓarf), attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿حديث﴾.
﴿يؤمنون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).

nahhas-irab:1-3.t: وَالْمُرْسَلاتِ عُرْفاً (1): Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned views on these verses, and we will add explanation and clarification. It was read before Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Ḥafṣ, from Yūsuf ibn Mūsā: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Muslim al-Baṭīn, from Abū al-ʿUbaydayn, from Ibn Masʿūd, on the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: وَالْمُرْسَلاتِ عُرْفاً (1) — he said: the winds. فَالْعاصِفاتِ عَصْفاً (2) — he said: the wind. وَالنَّاشِراتِ نَشْراً (3) — he said: the wind. Abū Jaʿfar said: it has also been related from Ibn Masʿūd that he said: الْمُرْسَلاتِ are the angels. The view that they are the winds is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū Ṣāliḥ, Mujāhid and Qatāda. And فَالْعاصِفاتِ are the winds — that is from three of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them. وَالنَّاشِراتِ: it has been related from Ibn Masʿūd that they are the angels; the first report, that it is the wind, is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās; and from Abū Ṣāliḥ that النَّاشِراتِ is the rain.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: From Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās: they are the angels. Saʿīd related from Qatāda: فَالْفارِقاتِ فَرْقاً — he said: the Quran, which distinguishes between truth and falsehood; and the construction on this view is: "by the distinguishing verses".

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
From Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās; they said: the angels. Qatāda said: the angels who deliver the Reminder to the prophets, peace be upon them. And from Abū Ṣāliḥ about some of these: he said: the prophets. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned that the adjective here has been put in place of the noun qualified, and for this reason the disagreement arose. If the construction is:
"by the Lord of the المرسلات", then the meaning is one, and the oath is by Allah, Mighty and Majestic. If we explain this further, we say: we have mentioned what has been said — that they are the winds, that they are the angels, and that they are the messengers, peace be upon them — and we have found no decisive proof that rules in favour of one of these views; so it must be referred back to the generality of the apparent meaning, and it is general for all of these things. عُرْفاً is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) if its meaning is "following one another"; and if its meaning is "and the angels sent with العرف", i.e. with Allah's command, obedience to Him and His books, then the construction is بالعرف, the bāʾ being dropped so the verb became transitive, as Sībawayh recited: [al-Basīṭ] 516-
أمرتك الخير فافعل ما أمرت به ... فقد تركتك ذا مال وذا نشب
(I have commanded you [to do] good, so do what you were commanded, for I have left you possessed of wealth and property.)
عَصْفاً, نَشْراً and فَرْقاً are maṣdars (verbal nouns) conveying emphasis. فَالْمُلْقِياتِ ذِكْراً: [ذِكْراً is] a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

nahhas-irab:6-6.t:
«[Translator's note: the first reading being described (عُذْراً أَوْ نُذْراً, with sukūn on both dhāls) has dropped out of the beginning of the entry.]» [This is] the reading of Abū ʿAmr, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī. The people of the two Sanctuaries, Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim read عُذْراً with a sukūn on the dhāl and «أو نذرا» with ḍamma on the dhāl. It is related from Zayd ibn Thābit and al-Ḥasan: «عذرا أو نذرا» with ḍamma on both dhāls. Giving both a sukūn is on the basis that they are both maṣdars (verbal nouns), as you say شكرته شكرا; and it may be that the original in both is the ḍamma, which was dropped because it was found heavy. Giving both ḍamma is on the basis that they are the plurals of عذير and نذير; and they may [also] be maṣdars, like شغلته شغلا. And عذير has the meaning of إعذار (excuse), as [the poet] said: [al-Wāfir] 517-
أريد حباءه ويريد قتلي ... عذيرك من خليلك من مراد
(I want to gift him, and he wants to kill me — who will excuse you for your friend from Murād?)
i.e. your excuse; and as [another] said: [al-Hazaj] 518-
نذير الحيّ من عدوان ... كانوا حيّة الأرض
(The warning of the tribe of ʿAdwān: they were the serpent of the land.)
Abū Jaʿfar said: these two verses are recited thus, in the accusative. Sībawayh recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 519-
عذيرك من مولى إذا نمت لم ينم ... يقول الخنا أو تعتريك زنابره
(Who will excuse you for a kinsman who, when you sleep, does not sleep, speaking obscenity, or his stings assail you?)
i.e. your excuse for this.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: I.e. of the resurrection, the reckoning and the requital. This is the apodosis (jawāb) of the oath. «ما» here means "that which" (الذي), written separately from «إنّ»; and it may not here be a separating [particle] with «لا» «[Translator's note: so in the source; perhaps «ما» meant as redundant/cancelling.]» redundant — do you not see that in its khabar (predicate) there is the lām confirming the khabar of إنّ? The hāʾ [the object pronoun] was dropped because of the length of the noun; the construction is: "that which you are promised — of the reckoning, the reward and the punishment — will surely occur".

nahhas-irab:8-8.t:
النجوم was put in the nominative by an implied verb like this one [i.e. طُمِسَتْ], because إذا here has the status of the particles of conditional requital. If someone says: Sībawayh said about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ بِما قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ إِذا هُمْ يَقْنَطُونَ [al-Rūm: 36], that «إذا» is an apodosis with the status of the fāʾ, and it only became an apodosis with the status of the fāʾ because one does not begin with it, just as one does not begin with the fāʾ; yet one has begun with it here, and you say إذا قمت قمت, beginning [with it]. Abū Jaʿfar said: I do not know of anyone who has faulted Sībawayh in this. The argument for him is that «إذا», when it is for surprise (mufājaʾa), one does not begin with it, as in His saying إِذا هُمْ يَقْنَطُونَ; and when it has the meaning of conditional requital, one begins with it. But Sībawayh has been opposed «[Translator's note: the source has «عوض», apparently «عورض».]» on the grounds that the fāʾ can enter upon it, so how can it be a substitute for it?
The answer is that it only enters [upon it] for emphasis. And the apodosis of فَإِذَا النُّجُومُ طُمِسَتْ is وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ; it has been said that the fāʾ is omitted; and it has been said that the apodosis is omitted.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read وَإِذَا الرُّسُلُ أُقِّتَتْ ] with hamza and a doubled qāf. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar the grammarian and Khālid ibn Ilyās read أُقِّتَتْ «[Translator's note: so vowelled in the source; the reading described is أُقِتَتْ.]» with hamza and a light qāf. Abū ʿAmr read «وقّتت» with wāw and a doubled qāf, and al-Ḥasan and Abū Jaʿfar read «وقتت» with wāw and a light qāf. Abū Jaʿfar said: the original in it is the wāw, because it is derived from الوقت (time); [Allah,] Mighty and Majestic, said: كانَتْ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ كِتاباً مَوْقُوتاً [al-Nisāʾ: 103] — this is from وقتت with a light [qāf]. But the ḍamma is found heavy on the wāw, so it is replaced by hamza. Sībawayh mentioned the two forms وقّتت and أقّتت without putting one before the other; so since both are eloquent, the more appropriate is to follow the written text.

nahhas-irab:12-13.t: لِيَوْمِ الْفَصْلِ: it has been said: the verb to which the lām is attached has been omitted, and the full stop is at لأي يوم أجّلت; then a verb was implied: "it was deferred to the Day of Decision". And it has been said: ليوم الفصل is a badal (substitute), with the lām repeated, like لِبُيُوتِهِمْ سُقُفاً مِنْ فِضَّةٍ [al-Zukhruf: 33] «[Translator's note: reference added by the translator.]». And it has been said: the lām means إلى ("to").

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: The first and second «ما» are in the position of rafʿ (nominative) as a mubtadaʾ (subject).

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: I.e. those who deny the Day of Resurrection and what is in it.

nahhas-irab:16-17.t: Al-Aʿraj read أَلَمْ نُهْلِكِ الْأَوَّلِينَ ثُمَّ نُتْبِعُهُمُ الْآخِرِينَ, putting نُتْبِعُهُمُ in the jussive «[Translator's note: i.e. نُتْبِعْهُمُ; the source prints the standard vowels.]», because it is conjoined to نهلك. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a solecism; and Abū Ḥātim said: this is a solecism; and Ismāʿīl mentioned that it is not permissible. Abū Jaʿfar said: «ثم» is one of the conjunctions, and [the question] concerns only the meaning; and in meaning it is not impossible, because it has been said about the meaning of أَلَمْ نُهْلِكِ الْأَوَّلِينَ that they are the people of Nūḥ, ʿĀd and Thamūd, and that the later ones are the people of Ibrāhīm ﷺ, the people of Madyan and Pharaoh. Abū Jaʿfar said: on this basis the reading with the jussive is sound.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: I.e. thus is My way with whoever persists in crime: that I destroy him for his crime.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: I.e. to whoever denies what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has informed, and His power over whatever He wills.

nahhas-irab:20-23.t:
Assimilating the qāf into the kāf [in نَخْلُقْكُمْ] is permissible. From Ibn ʿAbbās: «مهين» means weak. Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read فَقَدَرْنا light, and Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ and al-Kisāʾī read فَقَدَرْنا doubled «[Translator's note: i.e. فَقَدَّرْنا; the source prints the same vowels for both.]». The light form is more likely, because after it comes فَنِعْمَ الْقادِرُونَ and not المقدّرون; yet the reading with doubling is good, because it has been reported that they are two forms with one meaning: one says قدر and قدّره; and He said: نَحْنُ قَدَّرْنا بَيْنَكُمُ الْمَوْتَ [al-Wāqiʿa: 60]. It is not objectionable for two forms with one meaning to come in one place; He said: فَمَهِّلِ الْكافِرِينَ أَمْهِلْهُمْ رُوَيْداً [al-Ṭāriq: 17]. And the poet said: [al-Basīṭ] 520-
وأنكرتني وما كان الذي نكرت ... من الحوادث إلّا الشّيب والصّلعا
(She did not recognise me, and what she failed to recognise of the vicissitudes was nothing but grey hair and baldness.)
It has been said: the meaning of فقدرنا is [We determined] the drop, the clot and the lump of flesh. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: فقدرنا means "We had power over [it]".
فَنِعْمَ الْقادِرُونَ: [الْقادِرُونَ is] nominative by نعم, and the construction is: "how excellent are the determiners — We".

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: [Woe to the deniers] of the power of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, over these things and others.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: One says كفته when he gathers it and secures it; so the earth gathers people on its surface alive and in its belly dead. The derivation of this is from الكفتة, which is the container of a thing; and likewise الكفتة «[Translator's note: the source repeats the same word; the variant vowelling meant has been lost.]».

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: [أَحْياءً is] accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "We gather them in this state"; and it may be accusative because the action falls on it, i.e. "it gathers the living and the dead".

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: وَجَعَلْنا فِيها رَواسِيَ شامِخاتٍ: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: He says: lofty mountains. He said: وماءً فُراتاً: fresh. And ʿIkrima related from him: «ماء فراتا» means Sayḥān, Jayḥān, the Euphrates and the Nile; he said: and all fresh water in the world is from these four rivers.

nahhas-irab:28-29.t: انْطَلِقُوا إِلى ما كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تُكَذِّبُونَ (29), i.e. it will be said to them. Yaʿqūb al-Ḥaḍramī claimed that one of the readers read «انطلقوا» with fatḥa on the lām, as a past verb; as for the first, there was no disagreement about it.

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: لا ظَلِيلٍ is a naʿt (adjective) of ظلّ, i.e. not shading from the heat, and it does not protect from the flame of the Fire.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t:
إِنَّها تَرْمِي بِشَرَرٍ: [شَرَر is] the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz, as [the poet] said: [al-Wāfir] 521-
وتوقد ناركم شررا ويرفع ... لكم في كلّ مجمعة لواء
(Your fire is kindled into sparks, and a banner is raised for you at every gathering.)
and the dialect of Banū Tamīm is شرار. كَالْقَصْرِ is read in three ways «[Translator's note: the source prints the same vowels throughout; the readings meant are القَصْر, القَصَر and القِصَر.]»: the reading of the generality is كَالْقَصْرِ; from Ibn ʿAbbās and a group of his companions: كَالْقَصْرِ with fatḥa on the ṣād; and from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr there are two reports, in one of them كَالْقَصْرِ and in the other كَالْقَصْرِ. As was read before Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā, from Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq: Naṣr ibn ʿAlī said: Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us: Yūnus narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan: إنها ترمي بشرر كَالْقَصْرِ with kasra on the qāf. Naṣr said: and my father narrated to us: Yūnus narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan: بِشَرَرٍ كَالْقَصْرِ — he said: the stumps of palm trees. Abū Jaʿfar said: القصر with fatḥa on the qāf and sukūn on the ṣād — there are two views on its meaning. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: كَالْقَصْرِ — he said: He says: like the great palace. And likewise Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb said: it is a palace among palaces. Abū ʿUbayd said, from Ḥajjāj, from Hārūn; he said: القصر is thick firewood, like جمرة and جمر, and تمرة and تمر. Abū Jaʿfar said: sounder than this from al-Ḥasan is what was read before Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā, from Ismāʿīl, from Naṣr; he said: Yazīd narrated to us: Yūnus narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan; he said: «كالقصر» is the singular of القصور (palaces). Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a clear view; and the Arabs liken the she-camel and the camel to a palace, as [the poet] said: [al-Basīṭ] 522-
كأنها برج روميّ يشيّده ... بان بجصّ وآجرّ وأحجار
(As if she were a Byzantine tower, raised high by a builder with gypsum, baked bricks and stones.)
As for القصر [with fatḥa on the ṣād], Mujāhid and Qatāda said: it is the stumps of palm trees. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿĀbis related from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: القصر is the piece of timber three cubits long or more or less. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is the soundest thing said about it; and from it the fuller is called قصّار, because he works with timber like this. القصر in this sense is the plural of قصرة — and حاجة / حوج has been heard from the Arabs — and it may be the plural of قصرة, as حلقة / حلق has been heard. Someone said: الشرر is a plural and القصر a singular, so how could it be likened to it?
The answer is that it may be a singular that indicates a plural, or the plural of قصرة, or the act is meant, i.e. "like the great size of the palace". Al-Farrāʾ argued that it is preferable to read «كالقصر» with sukūn on the ṣād, because the verses are [rhymed] on this; do you not see that after it comes «صفر»? And he argued from the readers' reading of يَوْمَ يَدْعُ الدَّاعِ إِلى شَيْءٍ نُكُرٍ [al-Qamar: 6] with ḍamma on the kāf, because the verses are so, while in another place: فَحاسَبْناها حِساباً شَدِيداً وَعَذَّبْناها عَذاباً نُكْراً [al-Ṭalāq: 8] with sukūn on the kāf. He said: the readers agreed on giving a vowel to the first and a sukūn to the second. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is an ugly mistake: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kathīr read يَوْمَ يَدْعُ الدَّاعِ إِلى شَيْءٍ نُكُرٍ
with sukūn on the kāf «[Translator's note: the source prints نُكُرٍ with ḍamma; the reading described is نُكْرٍ.]». And what he brought regarding the agreement of verse-endings does not hold consistently and cannot be applied by analogy.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: «[Translator's note: the first reading described (جِمالَتٌ) has dropped out of the beginning of the entry.]» [This is] the reading of the people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash ibn ʿĪsā «[Translator's note: so in the source («الأعمش بن عيسى»), apparently a corruption.]», Ṭalḥa, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «كأنه جماله صفر» «[Translator's note: i.e. جِمالَةٌ.]»; and from Ibn ʿAbbās: «جمالات صفر» with ḍamma on the jīm. The first reading would be the plural of جمال or of جمالة; and جمالة is the plural of جمل, like حجر / حجارة. And جمالات may have the meaning of جمال, as one says رخل / رخال and ظئر / ظؤار; the tāʾ is for the feminine of the group. However, the exegetes say: they [جُمالات] are the ropes of ships — among them Ibn ʿAbbās and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr — except that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: pieces of copper. And it may be derived from الشيء المجمل (the thing gathered together).

nahhas-irab:35-35.t:
[هذا يَوْمُ لا يَنْطِقُونَ is] a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the readers agreed on the nominative of يوم. Abū Jaʿfar said:
This is close to what preceded. It is related from al-Aʿraj and al-Aʿmash that they read هذا يَوْمُ لا يَنْطِقُونَ in the accusative «[Translator's note: i.e. يَوْمَ; the source prints the nominative vowel.]». There are two views on its accusative. One is that it is an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. "this that we have mentioned is on this day". The other view, mentioned by al-Farrāʾ, is that «يوم» is indeclinable (mabnī). This is wrong according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh: in their view adverbs are not made indeclinable with the imperfect verb, because it is inflected; they are only made indeclinable with the past, as [the poet] said: [al-Ṭawīl] 523- على حين عاتبت المشيب على الصّبا (At the time when I reproached grey hair for [the loss of] youth.)

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: [فَيَعْتَذِرُونَ is] conjoined; and al-Farrāʾ claimed that the nominative was chosen in it so that the verse-endings agree.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: [هذا يَوْمُ الْفَصْلِ is] a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). جَمَعْناكُمْ وَالْأَوَّلِينَ: [الْأَوَّلِينَ is] conjoined (nasaq) to the kāf and mīm.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: The yāʾ [of فَكِيدُونِ] was dropped because the nūn became a compensation for it, since it has kasra, and it is at the end of a verse.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: Whoever gives kasra to the ʿayn [in عِيُونٍ] dislikes the ḍamma together with the yāʾ.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: The original is يشتهونه; the hāʾ, the noun [i.e. the pronoun], was dropped.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: I.e. this will be said to them.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: The kāf is in the position of naṣb (accusative), i.e. "a requital like that".

nahhas-irab:45-46.t: كُلُوا وَتَمَتَّعُوا قَلِيلًا is connected to what follows it «[Translator's note: so in the source («بما يليه»); in the sequence it relates to what precedes, verse 45.]», i.e. it was said to the deniers: كُلُوا وَتَمَتَّعُوا قَلِيلًا, i.e. for a short time and a little enjoyment.

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: Al-Farrāʾ said: [i.e.] and when they are told: "Pray". Others said: bowing was the hardest of things for the Arabs, to the point that some of them embraced Islam and refused to bow.

nahhas-irab:50-50.t: The bāʾ occurred before أي, even though the interrogative has the front of the sentence, because the prepositions with what follows them have the status of a single thing. Do you not see that your saying نظرت إلى زيد and نظرت زيدا have the same meaning?

safi-cedvel:1-7.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) the wāw of oath, and what follows it are conjunctions, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being أقسم; and (المرسلات) is a naʿt (adjective) standing in for the noun it qualifies, and likewise the following adjectives [Note: المرسلات, i.e. the winds that are sent, most probably, and likewise العاصفات and الناشرات; and الفارقات are the verses of the Noble Qur'an, and الملقيات are the angels..]; (عرفا) a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "in succession" [Note: It may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) if العرف is the opposite of النكر "what is disapproved", and then المرسلات means the angels.]; (العاصفات) conjoined to المرسلات, genitive like it; (عصفا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative; (الناشرات, الفارقات, الملقيات) nouns conjoined to المرسلات, genitive like it; (نشرا, فرقا) mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative; (ذكرا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle الملقيات, accusative; (عذرا) mafʿūl li-ajlihi, accusative, its governor being الملقيات [Note: Or it is a badal (substitute) of (ذكرا), accusative.]; (أو) a conjunction; (ما) relative noun, in the position of an accusative as the noun of إنّ; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis.
The clause «(أقسم) بالمرسلات ...» has no grammatical position: an opening clause (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «إنّ ما توعدون لواقع ...» has no grammatical position: the answer of the oath.
The clause «توعدون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).

* Morphology:
(1) المرسلات: plural of المرسل, passive participle of the four-letter verb أرسل; its pattern is مفعل, with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn; and المرسلات are the winds, or the angels, or the verses of the Noble Qur'an.
(عرفا): a noun for the hair of the horse above the neck (the mane); its pattern is فعل, with ḍamma then sukūn.. or it is a maṣdar meaning the opposite of النكر, or meaning succession; one says جاء القوم عرفا, i.e. one behind another. The word with ḍamma on the fāʾ has many other meanings..
(2) العاصفات: plural of العاصفة, feminine of العاصف.. see verse (22) of Surat Yūnus.
(عصفا): an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the triliteral عصف; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(3) الناشرات: plural of الناشرة, feminine of الناشر.. active participle of the triliteral نشر; its pattern is فاعل.
(نشرا): an aurally transmitted maṣdar of the triliteral نشر; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(4) الفارقات: plural of الفارقة, feminine of الفارق.. active participle of the triliteral فرق; its pattern is فاعل.
(فرقا): maṣdar of the triliteral فرق; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(5) الملقيات: plural of الملقية, feminine of الملقي, active participle of the four-letter verb ألقى; its pattern is مفعل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(6) نذرا: plural of النذير in the sense of الإنذار "warning", i.e. it is a maṣdar; or a noun meaning المنذر "the warner", i.e. in the sense of the active participle; its pattern is فعل, with ḍamma then sukūn.
(7) إنّما: written joined in the muṣḥaf, though it ought to be separate, because (ما) is a relative noun, not a maṣdar-forming particle nor a restraining one (kāffa).

safi-cedvel:8-13.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (إذا) an adverb, in the position of an accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied apodosis; (النجوم) fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb explained by the verb طمست, i.e. غابت "disappeared" or زالت "ceased", and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to النجوم; (إذا السماء) is like إذا النجوم, and the implied form of the omitted verb is تشقّقت or انشقّت "split" [Note: As in the saying of the Exalted in Surat al-Furqān: «ويوم تشقّق السماء ...», and in Surat al-Inshiqāq «إذا السماء انشقّت ...».]; (إذا الجبال) is like إذا النجوم, and the implied form of the omitted verb is تفتّتت "crumbled"; (إذا الرسل) is like إذا النجوم, and the implied form of the omitted verb is اجتمعت في الوقت المحدّد "gathered at the appointed time"; (لأيّ) attached to (أجّلت); (ليوم) attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being أجّلت..
The clause «(غابت) النجوم ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.. And the apodosis (jawāb) of إذا and what is conjoined to it is omitted, its implied form being: "judgment was passed between the creatures" or "the matter became clear".
The clause «طمست ...» has no grammatical position: explicative (tafsīriyya).
The clause «(تشقّقت) السماء ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «فرجت ...» has no grammatical position: explicative.
The clause «(تفتّتت) الجبال ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «نسفت ...» has no grammatical position: explicative.
The clause «(اجتمعت) الرسل ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «أقّتت ...» has no grammatical position: explicative.
The clause «أجّلت ...» is in the position of an accusative: the object of speech of an implied verb of saying [Note: This implied saying is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun of أقّتت.. or it is the apodosis of the first conditional (إذا), i.e. "when the stars are effaced.. it will be said".]

* Morphology:
(11) أقّتت: in it the wāw was changed into a hamza; its original form is وقّتت, and since the wāw had ḍamma it was changed into a hamza to bear the vowel.

safi-cedvel:14-15.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (ما) interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), in the position of a nominative [Note: The first interrogative is for deeming something remote, and the second for making it awesome.], in both places; (ويل) mubtadaʾ, nominative [Note: Beginning with an indefinite noun is permitted because the word is an imprecation.]; (يومئذ) an adverb of time, accusative — or indeclinable (mabnī) — annexed to an indeclinable adverbial noun, and the tanwīn in it compensates for an implied clause, i.e. "the day when judgment is passed between the creatures"; (للمكذّبين) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (ويل).
The clause «ما أدراك ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أدراك ...» is in the position of a nominative: khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ما).
The clause «ما يوم ...» is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the two objects of أدراك, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.
The clause «ويل ... للمكذّبين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

safi-cedvel:16-19.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for interrogation of affirmation (al-taqrīr), and (نهلك) is vowelled with kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; (ثمّ) a conjunction [Note: Or resumptive.. see verse (19) of Surat al-ʿAnkabūt.]..
The clause «نهلك ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «نتبعهم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
(كذلك) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), its governor being نفعل; (بالمجرمين) attached to (نفعل); (ويل.. للمكذّبين) is like the first [Note: The clause may be for emphasis, or to restrict the woe here to the punishment of this world and there to the punishment of the Hereafter — thus al-Bayḍāwī explained it —.].
The clause «نفعل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ويل ... للمكذّبين» has no grammatical position: resumptive, for emphasis.

safi-cedvel:20-24.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for interrogation of affirmation (al-taqrīr) [Note: I.e. for affirmation.. or it is for rebuke.]; (من ماء) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نخلقكم); (في قرار) attached to (جعلناه), by making it carry the meaning of وضعناه "We placed it"; (إلى قدر) attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ in (جعلناه), i.e. "deferred to a measure"..
The clause «نخلقكم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «جعلناه ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
(الفاء) conjunction in both places, and the one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) is omitted, its implied form being نحن; (ويل.. للمكذّبين) is like the first.
The clause «قدرنا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause — or to جعلناه —. The clause «نعم القادرون ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause قدرنا.
The clause «ويل ... للمكذّبين» has no grammatical position: resumptive, for emphasis..

safi-cedvel:25-28.t:
* I'rab:
(كفاتا) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (أحياء) mafʿūl bihi of (كفاتا) [Note: And (كفات) is the maṣdar of كفت, or it is an active participle, plural of كافت, like صائم and صيام.. or it is the object of an omitted verb, its implied form being تضمّ "it gathers", if (كفاتا) is a noun of place or a noun for the container in which something is gathered.]; (الواو) conjunction in both places; (فيها) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second mafʿūl bihi; (ماء) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (ويل.. للمكذّبين) is like the first.
The clause «نجعل الأرض ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «جعلنا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «أسقيناكم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «ويل ... للمكذّبين» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(كفاتا): an active participle, plural of كافت, or it is the maṣdar of the triliteral كفت, like حساب, or a noun for the place in which a thing is كفت, i.e. gathered.. Its pattern is فعال, with kasra on the fāʾ.
(شامخات): plural of شامخة, feminine of شامخ, active participle of the triliteral شمخ, meaning "it was high and lofty"; its pattern is فاعل.

* Rhetoric:
1- Indefiniteness (al-tankīr): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «أَحْياءً وَأَمْواتاً».
It says أحياء and أمواتا in the indefinite, though it (the earth) is the gatherer of all the living and the dead, and that is for magnification, as though it were said: it gathers living beings beyond counting and dead beyond reckoning; besides, the living and the dead of mankind are not all the living and the dead.
2- Indefiniteness: in the saying of Allah the Exalted «رَواسِيَ شامِخاتٍ» and «ماءً فُراتاً».
The benefit of the indefiniteness is to convey partitiveness, because in the sky there are mountains — Allah the Exalted said «وَيُنَزِّلُ مِنَ السَّماءِ مِنْ جِبالٍ فِيها مِنْ بَرَدٍ» — and in it there is sweet water too; indeed it is its source and its outflow. It may also be for magnification.

safi-cedvel:29-34.t:
* I'rab:
(إلى ما) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (انطلقوا); (به) attached to (تكذّبون); (إلى ظلّ) attached to the second (انطلقوا); (ذي) naʿt (adjective) of ظلّ, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (لا) negative; (ظليل) naʿt of ظلّ, genitive; the second (لا) negative; (من اللهب) attached to a naʿt of an implied object, i.e. "it does not ward off anything of the flame"; and the pronoun in (إنّها) refers to the Fire; (بشرر) attached to (ترمي); (كالقصر) attached to a naʿt of (شرر); (ويل.. للمكذّبين) is like the first.
The clause «انطلقوا ...» is in the position of an accusative: the object of speech of an implied verb of saying..
The clause «كنتم به تكذّبون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «تكذّبون ...» is in the position of an accusative: khabar (predicate) of كنتم.
The clause «انطلقوا (the second)» is in the position of an accusative: badal (substitute) of the first clause انطلقوا.
The clause «لا يغني ...» is in the position of a genitive: conjoined to the naʿt ظليل.
The clause «إنّها ترمي ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «ترمي ...» is in the position of a nominative: khabar of إنّ.
The clause «كأنّه جمالة ...» is in the position of a genitive: a second naʿt of شرر [Note: Or in the position of an accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) of الشرر, because it is particularized by the adjective.].
The clause «ويل ... للمكذّبين» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(30) شعب: plural of شعبة, a noun meaning a branch/division; its pattern is فعلة, with ḍamma then sukūn, and the plural is فعل, with ḍamma then fatḥa.
(31) اللهب: a noun for the tongue of fire; its pattern is فعل, with two fatḥas.
(32) شرر: a collective noun for what flies off from fire; its pattern is فعل, with two fatḥas, and the singular is شرارة, on the pattern فعالة, with fatḥa.
(33) جمالة: either a plural of جمل, like حجر and حجارة, on the pattern فعالة with kasra on the fāʾ.. or it is a collective noun..

* Rhetoric:
The unqualified simile (al-tashbīh al-mursal): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «إِنَّها تَرْمِي بِشَرَرٍ كَالْقَصْرِ كَأَنَّهُ جِمالَتٌ صُفْرٌ».
He likened the sparks, when they separate from the fire, in their hugeness, to the palace; and when they begin to rise and spread, because they split into countless numbers, to camels, so as to picture the splitting, the multitude, the yellowness and the particular movement. The order has been observed in the simile, and palaces and camels are likened to each other, so the second simile is an explanation of the first, in the sense that what first comes to mind from the likening to the palace was only hugeness.

safi-cedvel:35-37.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) negative in both places; (لهم) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (الفاء) conjunction [Note: It is a conjunction only, not causal, so the negation is directed at both the permission and the excusing.. If it were causal, the verb after it would be accusative. Moreover, the meaning may be taken as resumptive, i.e. they do offer excuses in some states of their speaking.]; (ويل.. للمكذّبين) is like the first. The clause «هذا يوم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ينطقون ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi. The clause «يؤذن لهم ...» is in the position of a genitive: conjoined to the clause ينطقون.
The clause «يعتذرون ...» is in the position of a genitive: conjoined to the clause يؤذن لهم.
The clause «ويل.. للمكذّبين» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Benefits:
- Detail and explanation:
In the saying of the Exalted (وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَهُمْ نارُ جَهَنَّمَ لا يُقْضى عَلَيْهِمْ فَيَمُوتُوا وَلا يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهُمْ مِنْ عَذابِها), ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read (فيموتون), conjoining it to يقضى, and Ibn Kharūf allowed resumption in it with the sense of causation. The Seven read (لا يُؤْذَنُ لَهُمْ فَيَعْتَذِرُونَ); the accusative was possible, like it in (فيموتوا), but it was avoided for the harmony of the verse-endings. The well-known view is that the sense of causation was not intended, but merely conjunction to the verb and including it with it in the thread of negation, because what is meant by (لا يُؤْذَنُ لَهُمْ) is the negation of permission to make excuses — and they were forbidden it in the saying of the Exalted (لا تَعْتَذِرُوا الْيَوْمَ) — so no excuse can come from them after that. Ibn Mālik Badr al-Dīn mentioned that it is resumptive, with the implied form (فهم يعتذرون), and that is problematic on the doctrine of the majority, because it entails that excusing is established while permission is negated, as in your saying (ما تؤذينا فنحبك) with the nominative. Abū al-Baqāʾ answered regarding the second analysis — i.e. resumption — by saying: i.e. (فهم يعتذرون), so the meaning is that they do not speak in a way that benefits them, i.e. they do not speak in some stations and speak in others; and it is not the answer to the negation, since if it were so the nūn would be dropped.

safi-cedvel:38-40.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (الأوّلين) conjoined to the pronoun of address in (جمعناكم), accusative; (الفاء) conjunction; (كان) a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (لكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of كان; (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and (النون) in (كيدون) is the nūn of protection (al-wiqāya) before the first-person yāʾ, which is omitted to suit the verse-ending; (ويل.. للمكذّبين) is like the first.
The clause «هذا يوم الفصل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «جمعناكم ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) [Note: Or in the position of an accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) of يوم الفصل, the linking pronoun being implied, and its governor being the demonstrative, i.e. "We gathered you in it".].
The clause «كان لكم كيد ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause هذا يوم..
The clause «كيدون ...» is in the position of a jussive (majzūm): the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «ويل ... للمكذّبين» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

safi-cedvel:41-45.t:
* I'rab:
(في ظلال) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of إنّ; (الواو) conjunction in the three places; (فواكه) conjoined to ظلال, genitive, and it is denied tanwīn because it is on the pattern of the furthest plurals (ṣīghat muntahā al-jumūʿ); (ممّا) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (فواكه)..
The clause «إنّ المتّقين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يشتهون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
(هنيئا) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of the fāʿil (agent) of كلوا and اشربوا; (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of a genitive, the returning pronoun being omitted, and the clause after it is the ṣila.]..
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كنتم..) is in the position of a genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (هنيئا), and (الباء) is causal.
(كذلك) attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), its governor being نجزي [Note: Because the reference is to the recompense, i.e. "We recompense the doers of good with a recompense like that recompense mentioned".]; (ويل.. للمكذّبين) is like the first.
The clause «كلوا ...» is in the position of an accusative: the object of speech of an implied verb of saying, i.e. "Allah says to them", or "the angels say: eat"..
The clause «اشربوا ...» is in the position of an accusative: conjoined to the clause كلوا. The clause «كنتم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «تعملون ...» is in the position of an accusative: khabar of كنتم.
The clause «إنّا ... نجزي» has no grammatical position: giving the reason (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «نجزى ...» is in the position of a nominative: khabar of إنّ.
The clause «ويل ... للمكذّبين» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(42) يشتهون: it contains a weak-letter change by quiescence (iʿlāl bi-l-taskīn) and a weak-letter change by deletion (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf); its original form is يشتهيون — with a yāʾ with ḍamma before the wāw: the ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt heavy, so it was made quiescent and the vowel was transferred to the hāʾ — a weak-letter change by quiescence —; two quiescent letters, the yāʾ and the wāw, met, so the yāʾ was deleted — a weak-letter change by deletion —; its pattern is يفتعون.

* Rhetoric:
The loose metaphor (al-majāz al-mursal): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي ظِلالٍ وَعُيُونٍ».
A loose metaphor whose relation is locality (al-maḥalliyya), namely Paradise, because the shades extend, the springs flow, and the fruits are ripe in it.

safi-cedvel:46-47.t:
* I'rab:
(قليلا) mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial), standing in for the adverb because it is its adjective, i.e. "a little time" [Note: It may be a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, i.e. "a little enjoyment".]; (ويل.. للمكذّبين) is like the first.
The clause «كلوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive, and the address is to the disbelievers in this world.
The clause «تمتّعوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «إنّكم مجرمون ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).

safi-cedvel:48-49.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (لهم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قيل); (لا) negative; (ويل.. للمكذّبين) is like the first.
The clause «قيل ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «اركعوا ...» is in the position of a nominative: the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) [Note: It is originally the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).].
The clause «لا يركعون ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «ويل ... للمكذّبين» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

safi-cedvel:50-50.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) linking the answer of an implied condition; (بأيّ) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يؤمنون); (بعده) an adverb, accusative, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (حديث).
The clause «يؤمنون ...» has no grammatical position: the answer of an implied condition, i.e. "if they do not believe in the Qur'an, then in what discourse after it will they believe?".

* Benefits:
- (أيّ) is a declinable noun, and it comes in five ways:
1- As a conditional: as in the saying of the Exalted: «أَيًّا ما تَدْعُوا فَلَهُ الْأَسْماءُ الْحُسْنى», (أَيَّمَا الْأَجَلَيْنِ قَضَيْتُ فَلا عُدْوانَ عَلَيَّ). 2- As an interrogative: as in the saying of the Exalted (أَيُّكُمْ زادَتْهُ هذِهِ إِيماناً), and the saying of the Exalted in the verse we are dealing with (فَبِأَيِّ حَدِيثٍ بَعْدَهُ يُؤْمِنُونَ).
3- As a relative: as in the saying of the Exalted ثُمَّ لَنَنْزِعَنَّ مِنْ كُلِّ شِيعَةٍ أَيُّهُمْ أَشَدُّ عَلَى الرَّحْمنِ عِتِيًّا, i.e. "the one who is most severe"; here it is indeclinable (mabnī) despite being annexed, and there is no harm in that.
4- To indicate the meaning of perfection, so it occurs as an adjective of an indefinite noun, as in (زيد رجل أيّ رجل) "Zayd is a man — what a man!", i.e. perfect in the qualities of men; and as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of a definite noun, as in (مررت بعبد الله أيّ رجل).
5- To be a link to the vocative of what has (ال), as in (يا أيها الرجل).

semin-durr:50-50.t: His saying: {فَبِأَيِّ حَدِيثٍ}: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to His saying «يُؤمنون», i.e. if they do not believe in this Qur'an, then in what thing will they believe? The majority read it in the third person (al-ghayba). Ibn ʿĀmir, in one transmission, and Yaʿqūb read it in the second person (al-khiṭāb), by way of iltifāt (shift of address) or of transition.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {عُرْفاً}: there are three aspects to it. The first: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. for the sake of al-ʿurf, which is the opposite of al-nukr (the reprehensible). What is meant by «المُرْسَلات» is either the angels, or the prophets, or the winds, i.e. by the angels sent forth, or the prophets sent forth, or the winds sent forth. And al-ʿurf is kindness (al-maʿrūf) and beneficence. The poet said:
4454 - مَنْ يَفْعَلِ الخيرَ لا يَعْدَمْ جَوازِيَهُ ... لا يَذْهَبُ العُرْفُ بينَ اللَّهِ والناسِ
(Whoever does good will not lack its rewards; kindness is not lost between Allah and people.)
It may be said: how did He pluralise the attribute of a rational masculine with alif and tāʾ, when it should properly be pluralised with wāw and nūn? You say «الأنبياءُ المُرْسَلونَ», and you do not say «المُرْسَلات». The answer is that «المُرْسَلات» is the plural of mursala, and mursala is an attribute of a group of prophets; so «المُرْسَلات» is the plural of «مُرْسَلة» occurring as an attribute of a group, not the plural of the singular «مُرْسَل». The second: that it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) in the sense of "successive", from their saying: they came like the mane (ʿurf) of a horse, and they are against so-and-so like the mane of a hyena, when they gang up against him. The third: that it is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. those sent with al-ʿurf.
There is weakness in this [last aspect]. The discussion of al-ʿurf preceded in al-Aʿrāf. The generality [of readers] have a sukūn on its rāʾ, and ʿĪsā [read it] with ḍamma; that is by making heavy what is light, as in «بَكُر» for bakr. It is possible that it is the original, with the well-known [reading] lightened from it, and it is possible that they are two independent patterns.

semin-durr:2-2.t: His saying: {عَصْفاً}: a maṣdar (verbal noun) emphasising the active participle. What is meant by «العاصفات» is the winds or the angels, likened to the winds in the swiftness of their course in the command of Allah the Exalted. Likewise «نَشْراً» and «فَرْقاً» are also accusative as maṣdars.

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {ذِكْراً}: a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), governed by «المُلْقِيات». The generality [of readers] read «فالمُلْقِياتِ» with a sukūn on the lām and a light qāf, an active participle. Ibn ʿAbbās [read it] with fatḥa on the lām and a doubled qāf, from al-talqiya, which is conveying speech to the one addressed. al-Mahdawī also narrated from him fatḥa on the qāf, a passive participle, i.e. cast from the side of Allah the Exalted.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {عُذْراً أَوْ نُذْراً}: there are several aspects to them. The first: they are two badals (substitutes) from «ذِكْراً». The second: they are accusative by it as objects, and making a maṣdar with tanwīn govern is permissible; among it is {أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ يَتِيماً} [al-Balad: 14-15]. The third: they are mafʿūl li-ajlihi (objects of purpose), and what governs them is either «المُلْقِيات» or «ذِكْراً», because each of them is fit to be caused by one of the two. In that case two aspects are permissible in «عُذْراً» and «نُذْراً»: the first, that they are maṣdars with a quiescent middle radical, like al-shukr and al-kufr; the second, that they are the plurals of ʿadhīr and nadhīr, by which the maṣdar is meant, in the sense of excusing (iʿdhār) and warning (indhār), like al-nakīr in the sense of al-inkār. The fourth: they are accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «المُلْقِيات» or from the pronoun in it. In that case they may be maṣdars occurring in the place of a ḥāl by the well-known interpretation in such cases; or plurals of ʿadhīr and nadhīr by which the maṣdar is meant, or by which the active participle is meant in the sense of al-muʿdhir and al-mundhir, i.e. excusing or warning.
The generality [of readers] read with a sukūn on the dhāl of «عُذْراً» and «نُذْراً». Zayd ibn Thābit, Ibn Khārija and Ṭalḥa read with ḍamma on it; and the two Ḥaramīs [Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr], Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr with sukūn in «عُذْراً» and ḍamma in «نُذُراً». The sukūn and ḍamma are as preceded, in that each of them may be the origin of the other, or they may be two independent origins; and each of the heavy and the light may be a maṣdar, or a plural whose middle radical was made quiescent for lightness. Ibrāhīm al-Taymī read «عُذْراً ونُذْراً» with the conjunctive wāw in place of «أو», which indicates that «أو» is in the sense of the wāw.

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {إِنَّ مَا تُوعَدُونَ}: this is the apodosis of the oath in His saying «والمُرْسَلاتِ», and what follows it is conjoined to it, not an independent oath, for what preceded at the beginning of this work, and because the fāʾ occurs as a conjunction, since it is not [a particle] of oath. «ما» is a relative noun in the sense of «الذي», the noun of «إنَّ», and «تُوْعَدون» is its ṣila (relative clause), the returning pronoun being omitted, i.e. that which you are promised. And «لَواقعٌ» is its khabar. «إنَّ» should properly have been written separate from the relative «ما», but they wrote it joined to it.

semin-durr:8-8.t: His saying: {فَإِذَا النجوم طُمِسَتْ}: «النجومُ» is nominative by an implied verb explained by what follows it, according to the Basrans other than al-Akhfash; and as mubtadaʾ (subject) according to the Kufans and al-Akhfash. Regarding the apodosis of «إذا» there are two views. The first: it is omitted, its implied form being: when the stars are obliterated, what you are promised will occur — because of the indication of His saying «إنَّ ما تُوْعَدُوْن لَواقعٌ» — or: the matter will become clear. The second: it is {لأَيِّ يَوْمٍ أُجِّلَتْ}, on the implying of a verb of saying, i.e. it will be said: for what day ...; so the verb [of saying] is in reality the apodosis. It was also said: the apodosis is «ويلٌ يومئذٍ»; Makkī transmitted it, and it is a mistake, because if it were the apodosis the fāʾ would be required for it, since it is a nominal clause.

semin-durr:11-11.t: His saying: {أُقِّتَتْ}: Abū ʿAmr read «وُقِّتَتْ» with the wāw, and the rest «أُقِّتَتْ» with a hamza in place of the wāw. They said: [the wāw] is the original, because it is from al-waqt (time), and the hamza is a substitute for it because it has a permanent ḍamma. Mention of this has preceded at the beginning of this work.

semin-durr:12-12.t: His saying: {لأَيِّ يَوْمٍ}: attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أُجِّلَتْ». This clause is governed by an implied verb of saying, i.e. it will be said. This implied saying may be the apodosis of «إذا», as preceded, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nominative of «أُقِّتَتْ», i.e. it being said concerning them: for what day were they deferred?

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {لِيَوْمِ الفصل}: a badal (substitute) from «لأيِّ يومٍ», with repetition of the governing element. It was also said: rather, it is attached to an implied verb, i.e. they were deferred to the Day of Decision. It was also said: the lām is in the sense of «إلى»; Makkī mentioned both.

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {وَيْلٌ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject); what permits beginning with it [though indefinite] is its being an imprecation. al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you say: how did the indefinite occur as mubtadaʾ in His saying "وَيْلٌ"? I say: in its origin it is an accusative maṣdar standing in place of its verb, but it was diverted to the nominative to indicate the permanence and continuance of the meaning of destruction for those imprecated against; similar to it is {سَلاَمٌ عَلَيْكُمْ} [al-Anʿām: 54]. "وَيْلاً له" in the accusative is permissible, but it was not read so.» I say: what he mentioned is not among the justifications [for an indefinite mubtadaʾ] that the grammarians enumerated; the justification is only what I mentioned to you, its being an imprecation. The benefit of diverting it to the nominative is what he mentioned. And «يومئذٍ» is an adverb (ẓarf) for «الوَيْل». Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted it to be an attribute of «وَيْلٌ», with «للمُكَذِّبين» its khabar (predicate).

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {أَلَمْ نُهْلِكِ}: the generality [of readers] have ḍamma on the imperfect prefix, from the quadriliteral «أَهْلَكَ». Qatāda [read it] with fatḥa. al-Zamakhsharī said: «From halakahu, in the sense of ahlakahu (he destroyed him). al-ʿAjjāj said:
4455 - ومَهْمَهٍ هالكِ مَنْ تعرَّجا
(And many a desert waste, destroyer of whoever turns aside into it.)»
I say: so «مَنْ» is governed by «هالك», and it is from halaka. However, some people made this a proof for the resembling adjective (al-ṣifa al-mushabbaha) governing a relative noun, and made it from the intransitive, because the condition of the resembling adjective is that it be from an intransitive verb; on this basis there is no proof in it.

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {ثُمَّ نُتْبِعُهُمُ}: the generality [of readers] have the ʿayn in the nominative, as resumptive, i.e. then We shall make them follow; so Abū al-Baqāʾ rendered it [as "then We, We make them follow"]. He said: «It is not conjoined, because conjunction would require the meaning to be: We destroyed the former ones, then We made the later ones follow them in destruction; and it is not so, because the destruction of the later ones has not yet occurred.» I say: in the resumptive aspect there is no need to posit a mubtadaʾ before the verb; rather, the verb is made conjoined to the whole clause of His saying «ألم نُهْلِك». This resumption is indicated by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh «ثم سَنُتْبِعُهم» with the sīn of futurity.
al-Aʿraj, and al-ʿAbbās from Abū ʿAmr, read it with a sukūn. There are two aspects to it. The first: it is making the nominative quiescent, so it is resumptive like the overtly nominative. The second: it is conjoined to a jussive. Those meant by "the later ones" are then the people of Shuʿayb, Lūṭ and Mūsā, and by "the former ones" the people of Nūḥ, ʿĀd and Thamūd.

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {كَذَلِكَ نَفْعَلُ}: i.e. like that hideous act, We do with everyone who commits crimes.

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying: {فَقَدَرْنَا}: Nāfiʿ and al-Kisāʾī read it with doubling (shadda), from al-taqdīr (determining), which agrees with His saying: {مِن نُّطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ} [ʿAbasa: 19]. The rest [read it] light, from al-qudra (power); this is indicated by His saying «فنِعْمَ القادِرون». On the first reading the meaning may be: how excellent are We who are able to determine it; and if «القادِرون» is made in the sense of «المُقَدِّرُون», it is a combination of two words whose meaning is one. Among this is His saying, Exalted is He: {فَمَهِّلِ الكافرين أَمْهِلْهُمْ رُوَيْداً} [al-Ṭāriq: 17], and the saying of al-Aʿshā:
4456 - وأَنْكَرَتْني وما كان الذي نَكِرَتْ ... من الحوادِث إلاَّ الشَّيْبَ والصَّلعَا
(She did not recognise me, and what she found strange among the vicissitudes was nothing but grey hair and baldness.)

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {كِفَاتاً}: al-kifāt is a name for the container in which something is gathered (yukfatu), i.e. collected; Abū ʿUbayda said this. One says: kafatahu yakfituhu, i.e. he gathered it and drew it together. In the ḥadīth: «Gather in (ikfitū) your children.» al-Ṣamṣāma ibn al-Ṭirimmāḥ said:
4457 - وأنتَ اليوم فوقَ الأرضِ حَيّاً ... وأنتَ غداً تَضُمُّك في كِفاتِ
(Today you are alive upon the earth, and tomorrow it will hold you in a container.)
It was also said: al-kifāt is a name for what gathers, like al-ḍimām and al-jimāʿ; one says: this chapter is the jimāʿ (comprehensive gathering) of the chapters. Regarding its accusative there are two aspects. The first: it is the second object of «نَجْعَلْ», because it is [a verb] of transformation (taṣyīr). The second: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الأرضَ», with the second object being «أحياءً وأمواتاً», in the sense of: did We not make it living with plants and dead without plants, i.e. part of it so and part of it so. It was also said: kifāt is the plural of kāfit, like ṣiyām and qiyām as plurals of ṣāʾim and qāʾim. It was also said: rather, it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), like al-kitāb and al-ḥisāb.

semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying: {أَحْيَآءً}: there are several aspects to it. The first: it is accusative by «كِفات»; Makkī said this, and al-Zamakhsharī, who began with it — after having made «كِفاتاً» the name of what gathers, as in their saying al-ḍimām and al-jimāʿ. This prevents «كِفاتاً» from governing «أحياءً» in the accusative, because it is not one of the governing nouns. Likewise if we make it in the sense of the container, according to the view of Abū ʿUbayda, it does not govern either; the grammarians have explicitly stated that nouns of place, time and instrument, even if they are derived and run on the pattern of verbs, do not govern, such as marmā and minjal; and regarding the noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar) there is a well-known disagreement. Their accusative by «كِفات» only works according to the view of Abū al-Baqāʾ, for he permitted only that it be the plural of an active participle or a maṣdar, and both are governing nouns.
The second aspect: that it is accusative by an implied verb indicated by «كِفات», i.e. it gathers them living on its back and dead in its belly; al-Zamakhsharī gave this second.
The third: that the two are accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الأرضَ» with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. possessing living and dead.
