The fourth: that the two are accusative as a ḥāl from something omitted, i.e. it gathers you living and dead, because it is known that it is a container for humans; al-Zamakhsharī said this, and Makkī inclined to it, except that he rendered it in the third person, i.e. the earth gathers them in these two states.
The fifth: that the two are accusative as the second object of «نَجْعل», with «كِفاتاً» a ḥāl, as its establishment preceded. The indefiniteness of «أحياءً وأمواتاً» is either for magnification, i.e. it gathers living who cannot be estimated and dead who cannot be counted; or for partitiveness, because the living and the dead of humans are not all the living nor all the dead. Likewise the indefiniteness in «ماءً فُراتاً» admits both meanings too: as for magnification, it is clear, because of the greatness of the favour of it upon them; as for partitiveness, it is like His saying, Exalted is He: {وَيُنَزِّلُ مِنَ السمآء مِن جِبَالٍ فِيهَا مِن بَرَدٍ} [al-Nūr: 43], which conveys partitiveness, and the Qurʾān explains itself.
And al-shāmikhāt is the plural of «شامِخ», which is the very lofty; from it is «شَمَخَ بأَنْفِه» (he raised his nose) when he was arrogant; it was made a metonymy for that, like "turning the side" and "turning the cheek", even if none of that actually takes place.

semin-durr:29-29.t: His saying: {انطلقوا}: i.e. that will be said to them. The generality [of readers] read the second «انطَلِقوا» like the first, in the imperative form, for emphasis. Ruways from Yaʿqūb [read] «انطلَقوا» with fatḥa on the lām, a past verb, as a statement, i.e. when they were commanded, they complied with that. This is a place for the fāʾ, so the construction should have been «فانطَلَقوا», as in your saying: I said "Go" and he went; the absence of the fāʾ here is not clear.

semin-durr:31-31.t: His saying: {لاَّ ظَلِيلٍ}: an attribute of «ظلٍّ», and «لا» comes between the attribute and the thing described to convey negation. The first attribute was brought as a noun and the second as a verb, to indicate the negation of the established and settled presence of this attribute for the shade, and the negation of the renewal and occurrence of availing against the flame.

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying: {إِنَّهَا}: i.e. Jahannam, because the whole context is about it. The generality [of readers] read «بَشرَرٍ» with fatḥa on the shīn and no alif between the two rāʾs; Warsh thins (yuraqqiqu) the first rāʾ because of the kasra of the one after it. Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Miqsam read with kasra on the shīn and an alif between the two rāʾs; and ʿĪsā likewise, except that he gave the shīn fatḥa. The reading of Ibn ʿAbbās may be the plural of sharara, faʿala being pluralised on fiʿāl, as in raqaba and riqāb, raḥaba and riḥāb; or it may be the plural of sharr not meant as the elative of preference (afʿal al-tafḍīl): one says rajulun sharrun and rijālun shirār, rajulun khayrun and rijālun khiyār, and both take the feminine, so one says imraʾatun sharra and imraʾatun khayra. If preference is meant by them, that is impossible for both, and they are subject to rules mentioned in the books of the grammarians. That is: it throws evil ones (shirār) of punishment, or evil ones of creation.
As for the reading of ʿĪsā, it is the plural of sharāra with the alif, and that is the dialect of Tamīm. al-Sharara and al-sharāra are what flies off from the fire scattered (sparks).
His saying: {كالقصر}: the generality [of readers] have fatḥa on the qāf and sukūn on the ṣād, and it is the well-known palace (qaṣr); [the sparks] are likened to it in size and greatness. Ibn ʿAbbās and his two students Ibn Jubayr and Ibn Jabr, and al-Ḥasan, [read] with fatḥa on the qāf and the ṣād; it is the plural of qaṣara with fatḥa, and al-qaṣara is the necks of camels and of palm trees, and the stumps of trees. Ibn Jubayr and al-Ḥasan also read with kasra on the qāf and fatḥa on the ṣād, the plural of «قَصَرة», meaning with fatḥa on the qāf. al-Zamakhsharī said: «Like ḥāja and ḥiwaj», and the Shaykh said: «Like ḥalaqa (a ring) of iron and ḥilaq.» And «كالقَصِرِ» was read with fatḥa on the qāf and kasra on the ṣād, and I have not seen a justification for it. It appears that it is of the type of itbāʿ (vowel harmony): the origin is «كالقَصْرِ» with a quiescent ṣād, then the ṣād was made to follow the vowel of the rāʾ, so it was given kasra. And if they have done that with what is occupied by a vowel, as in katif and kabid, then for them to do it with what is free of a vowel is all the more fitting. It may also be through transfer (naql), in the sense that he paused on the word and transferred the kasra of the rāʾ to the quiescent letter before it, then treated the connected reading like the pause; this is a widespread type among the readers and grammarians. ʿAbd Allāh read it with ḍamma on both. There are two aspects to it. The first: it is the plural of qaṣr, like rahn and ruhun; al-Zamakhsharī said this. The second: it is shortened from quṣūr, as in [the poet's] saying:
4458 - فيها عيايِيْلُ أُسودٍ ونُمُرْ
(In it are prowling lions and leopards.)
He means numūr, but shortened it; and as in his saying «النُّجُم», meaning al-nujūm. al-Zamakhsharī's derivation is preferable, because the place of the second is either poetic necessity or rarity.

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying: {جِمَالَةٌ}: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Ḥafṣ read «جِمالَةٌ», and the rest «جِمالات». Regarding «الجِمالَة» there are two aspects. The first: it is an explicit plural, the tāʾ being for the feminine of the plural; one says jamal, jimāl and jimāla, like dhakar, dhikār and dhikāra, and ḥajar and ḥijāra. The second: it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ), like al-dhikāra and al-ḥijāra; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, and the first is the view of the grammarians. As for «جِمالات», it may be the plural of this «جِمالة», or the plural of jimāl, so it would be a plural of a plural. It may also be the plural of the singular jamal, as in their saying «رجِالات قريش» — so they said. This is questionable, because they explicitly stated that non-rational primitive (jāmid) nouns are not pluralised with alif and tāʾ unless they have no broken plural; if they have a broken plural, they are not [so] pluralised. They said: for that reason al-Mutanabbī was declared to have erred in his saying:
4459 - إذا كان بعضُ الناسِ سَيْفاً لدولةٍ ... ففي الناسِ بُوْقاتٌ لها وطُبولُ
(If some people are a sword for a dynasty, then among people there are trumpets and drums for it.)
For he pluralised «بُوق» as «بُوقات» although they say «أَبْواق»; likewise «جِمالات» although they say jamal and jimāl. Moreover, some do not permit that at all and consider the likes of ḥammāmāt and sijillāt anomalous, even though they have no broken plural.
Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, Ibn Jubayr, Qatāda and Abū Rajāʾ — with disagreement [in transmission] from them — read it likewise, except that they gave the jīm ḍamma; these are the ropes of ships. It was also said: the cables of bridges, the singular being «جُمْلة», because it comprises strands of ropes. There are two aspects to it. The first: that «جُمالات» be the plural of jumāl, and jumāl the plural of jumla — so the Shaykh said; but establishing that jumāl with ḍamma is the plural of jumla with ḍamma needs transmission. The second: that «جُمالات» be the plural of jumāla; al-Zamakhsharī said this, and it is apparent. Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Sulamī and Abū Ḥaywa read «جُمالة» with ḍamma on the jīm, and this supports what al-Zamakhsharī just said.
His saying: {صُفْرٌ}: an attribute of «جِمالات» or of «جِمالة», because it is either a plural or a collective noun. The generality [of readers] have a sukūn on the fāʾ, plural of ṣafrāʾ, and al-Ḥasan [read] with ḍamma on it, as if it were itbāʿ (vowel harmony). The simile here is of the utmost eloquence. al-Zamakhsharī said: «It was said: "ṣufr" means black tending to yellow. In the poetry of ʿImrān ibn Ḥiṭṭān the Khārijite:
4460 - دَعَتْهُمْ بأعلَى صوتِها ورَمَتْهُمُ ... بمثل الجِمال الصفر نَزَّاعةِ الشَّوى
(It called them with its loudest voice and pelted them with the like of yellow camels, stripping off the scalps.)
And Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Maʿarrī said:
4461 - حمراءُ ساطِعَةُ الذوائب في الدُّجَى ... تَرْمي بكل شَرارةٍ كطِرافٍ
(Red, its flames shining in the darkness, it throws every spark like a leather tent.)
So he likened it to al-ṭirāf, which is a tent of leather, in greatness and redness; it seems he intended, in his wickedness, to outdo the simile of the Qurʾān. And in his self-satisfaction at the imagined surpassing that was made attractive to him, he brought at the beginning of his verse the word "حمراءُ" (red), as preparation for it, proclaiming it and alerting the hearers to its place. He was blind — may Allah combine for him the blindness of both abodes — to His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: "كأنه جِمالةٌ صُفْرٌ", which is equivalent to saying "like a red tent". Moreover, in the likening to the qaṣr, which is the fortress, there is likening from two aspects: in respect of greatness and in respect of height in the air; and in the likening to the jimālāt, which are the cables, there is likening from three aspects: length, greatness and yellowness» — end of quote. A little before that he had said: «They are likened to palaces, then to camels, to make the simile clear; do you not see that they liken camels to al-afdān?» I say: al-afdān are palaces, and it is as though he is alluding to the saying of ʿAntara:
4462 - فوقَفْتُ فيها ناقتي وكأنَّها ... فَدَنٌ لأَقْضِيَ حاجةَ المُتَلَوِّمِ
(So I halted my she-camel there, and she was like a palace, that I might fulfil the need of one who lingers.)

semin-durr:35-35.t: His saying: {هذا يَوْمُ لاَ يَنطِقُونَ}: the generality [of readers] have «يومُ» in the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of «هذا». Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Aʿraj, al-Aʿmash, Abū Ḥaywa, and ʿĀṣim in some of his chains, [read it] with fatḥa. There are two aspects to it. The first: the fatḥa is a fatḥa of indeclinability (bināʾ), and it is the khabar of «هذا», as has preceded. The second: it is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), occurring as the khabar of «هذا», on the basis that [«هذا»] points to the threat that preceded, as if it were said: this punishment mentioned will be on a day on which they do not speak. Something similar to this preceded at the end of al-Māʾida in His saying: {هذا يَوْمُ يَنفَعُ}, except that the accusative there is mutawātir.

semin-durr:36-36.t: His saying: {وَلاَ يُؤْذَنُ}: the generality [of readers] have it with the agent unnamed (passive). al-Ahwāzī related from Zayd ibn ʿAlī «ولا يَأْذَنُ», naming the agent, who is Allah the Exalted. Regarding the nominative of «فيعتذرون» there are two aspects. The first: it is resumptive, i.e. so they make excuses. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «The meaning would be that they do not speak with speech that benefits them, or they speak at some stations and do not speak at others.» The second: it is conjoined to «يُؤْذن», so it is negated; «had it been put in the accusative, it would have been caused by it.» Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «It was not put in the accusative as the answer to the negation because of the resemblance of the verse-endings; both aspects are permissible» — end of quote. So he made the impossibility of the accusative merely a matter of verbal correspondence, and the apparent sense of this, together with his saying «both aspects are permissible», is that they have one meaning; but it is not so — rather, the nominative has a meaning other than the meaning of the accusative. al-Aʿlam held a view like this, that the verb may be put in the nominative while its meaning is that of the accusative, and Ibn ʿUṣfūr refuted him.

semin-durr:41-41.t: His saying: {فِي ظِلاَلٍ}: this is the reading of the generality, the plural of ẓill. al-Aʿmash [read] «ظُلَلٍ», the plural of ẓulla. Its like preceded in Yā Sīn, except that both [readings] there are mutawātir.

semin-durr:43-43.t:
His saying: {كُلُواْ}: governed by a verb of saying; that saying is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in the adverbial phrase, i.e. being in shades, it being said to them that. Likewise {كُلُواْ وَتَمَتَّعُواْ قَلِيلاً}: if that is said to them in this world, it is clear; and if it is said in the Hereafter, it is a reminder of their state, i.e. they deserve to have been told such-and-such in their worldly life. Its like:
4463 - إخْوَتي لا تَبْعَدُوا أبداً ... وبَلَى واللَّهِ قد بَعِدُوا
(My brothers, may you never perish! — and yes, by Allah, they have perished.)
That is: they are worthy of having that prayer made for them.

ukberi-tibyan:1-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالْمُرْسَلَاتِ عُرْفًا (١) فَالْعَاصِفَاتِ عَصْفًا (٢) وَالنَّاشِرَاتِ نَشْرًا (٣) فَالْفَارِقَاتِ فَرْقًا (٤) فَالْمُلْقِيَاتِ ذِكْرًا (٥) عُذْرًا أَوْ نُذْرًا (٦)).
The first wāw is for the oath, and those after it are for conjunction; that is why the fāʾ comes. (عُرْفًا) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. following one another — meaning the winds.
It is also said that what is meant is the angels, in which case the implied form is «بِالْعُرْفِ» (with what is good) or «لِلْعُرْفِ» (for what is good).
(عَصْفًا) is an emphatic maṣdar (mafʿūl muṭlaq, absolute object). (ذِكْرًا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
There are two views on (عُذْرًا أَوْ نُذْرًا). First: they are two maṣdars whose middle letter may be vowelless or take a ḍamma.
Second: they are the plurals of «عَذِير» and «نَذِير». On the first view they are accusative as mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), or as a badal (substitute) for «ذِكْرًا», or [as objects] of «ذِكْرًا». On the second view they are two ḥāls from the pronoun in «الْمُلْقِيَاتِ», i.e. excusing and warning.

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّمَا تُوعَدُونَ لَوَاقِعٌ (٧)).
The words of the Exalted (إِنَّمَا): «مَا» here means «الَّذِي» (that which), and the khabar (predicate) is «لَوَاقِعٌ». «مَا» cannot be maṣdariyya here, nor the restraining «مَا» (kāffa).

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَإِذَا النُّجُومُ طُمِسَتْ (٨)).
The words of the Exalted (فَإِذَا النُّجُومُ): the apodosis (jawāb) of «إِذَا» is omitted, its implied form being: the matter became clear, or was decided; or: it will be said (لِأَيِّ يَوْمٍ); and its apodosis is what governs it. (طُمِسَتْ) cannot be the apodosis, because it is the verb that explains [the verb required in] the position of «النُّجُوم», so the statement is not completed by it; the implied form is «فَإِذَا طُمِسَتِ النُّجُومُ» (when the stars are effaced), then the verb was omitted, being dispensed with by what follows. The Kufans said: the noun after «إِذَا» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); this is far-fetched, because of the conditional sense in «إِذَا», which demands a verb.

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا الرُّسُلُ أُقِّتَتْ (١١)).
The words of the Exalted (وُقِّتَتْ): with a wāw according to the original form, because it is from «الْوَقْت» (time).
It has also been read without doubling (وُقِتَتْ), and this is supported by the words of the Exalted (كِتَابًا مَوْقُوتًا).
It has also been read with a hamza (أُقِّتَتْ), because the wāw carries an inherent ḍamma, so the hamza was resorted to in order to avoid it.

ukberi-tibyan:12-13.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لِأَيِّ يَوْمٍ أُجِّلَتْ (١٢) لِيَوْمِ الْفَصْلِ (١٣)).
The words of the Exalted (لِأَيِّ يَوْمٍ): i.e. it will be said to them. (لِيَوْمِ الْفَصْلِ) is an explanation of what precedes it.

ukberi-tibyan:15-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ (١٥)).
The words of the Exalted (وَيْلٌ): it is a mubtadaʾ (subject). (يَوْمَئِذٍ) is a naʿt (adjective) of it, or an adverb (ẓarf) for it. (لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ) is the khabar (predicate).

ukberi-tibyan:16-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَمْ نُهْلِكِ الْأَوَّلِينَ (١٦) ثُمَّ نُتْبِعُهُمُ الْآخِرِينَ (١٧)).
The words of the Exalted (ثُمَّ نُتْبِعُهُمُ): the majority read it in the nominative, i.e. «ثُمَّ نَحْنُ نُتْبِعُهُمْ» (then We shall make them follow); it is not conjoined [to «نُهْلِكِ»], because conjunction would require the meaning to be: We destroyed the criminals, then made the later ones follow them in destruction; and that is not so, because the destruction of the later ones has not yet happened. It has also been read, irregularly, with a sukūn on the ʿayn (نُتْبِعْهُمُ), and there are two views on it. First: it is by lightening, not by the jussive. Second: it is jussive, and the meaning is: then We made the later ones follow them in the promise of destruction; or by «الْآخِرِينَ» He meant the last of those who were destroyed.

ukberi-tibyan:22-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِلَى قَدَرٍ مَعْلُومٍ (٢٢) فَقَدَرْنَا فَنِعْمَ الْقَادِرُونَ (٢٣)).
The words of the Exalted (إِلَى قَدَرٍ): it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. deferred until a known measure.
(قَدَرْنَا), without doubling, is better, because of the words of the Exalted «فَنِعْمَ الْقَادِرُونَ», and He did not say «الْمُقَدِّرُونَ». Whoever doubles the verb (قَدَّرْنَا) points to multiplicity, and that dispenses with expressing multiplicity by doubling the noun. The one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) is omitted, i.e. «فَنِعْمَ الْقَادِرُونَ نَحْنُ» (how excellent are the determiners — We).

ukberi-tibyan:25-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ كِفَاتًا (٢٥) أَحْيَاءً وَأَمْوَاتًا (٢٦)).
The words of the Exalted (كِفَاتًا): it is the plural of «كَافِت» (one who gathers), like «صَائِم» and «صِيَام». It is also said that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), like «كِتَاب» and «حِسَاب», and the implied form is «ذَاتُ كَفْتٍ» (possessed of gathering), i.e. of collecting. As for «أَحْيَاءً», there are two views on it. First: it is the object of «كِفَاتًا».
Second: it is the second object of «جَعَلْنَا»: [We made] part of the earth living with plants; on this view «كِفَاتًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:27-27.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَسْقَيْنَاكُمْ مَاءً فُرَاتًا (٢٧)).
The tāʾ in «فُرَات» (sweet water) is a root letter.

ukberi-tibyan:30-33.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (انْطَلِقُوا إِلَى ظِلٍّ ذِي ثَلَاثِ شُعَبٍ (٣٠) لَا ظَلِيلٍ وَلَا يُغْنِي مِنَ اللَّهَبِ (٣١) إِنَّهَا تَرْمِي بِشَرَرٍ كَالْقَصْرِ (٣٢) كَأَنَّهُ جِمَالَةٌ صُفْرٌ (٣٣)).
The words of the Exalted (لَا ظَلِيلٍ): a naʿt (adjective) of «ظِلٍّ».
(الْقَصْرُ) with a sukūn on the ṣād — this is the well-known reading — is the building [i.e. palace].
It is also read with a fatḥa on it (الْقَصَر), and it is then the plural of «قَصَرَة», which is the base of a palm tree or of a tree.
(جِمَالَاتٌ) is the plural of «جِمَالَة», which is a collective noun, like «الذِّكَارَة» and «الْحِجَارَة»; and the ḍamma (جُمَالَات) is a dialectal form.

ukberi-tibyan:35-35.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هَذَا يَوْمُ لَا يَنْطِقُونَ (٣٥)).
The words of the Exalted (هَذَا): it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (يَوْمُ لَا يَنْطِقُونَ) is its khabar (predicate).
It is also read with a fatḥa on the mīm (يَوْمَ), and it is then accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. this which has been mentioned is on the day when they will not speak. The Kufans allowed it to be nominative in position and indeclinable in form, because it is annexed to a clause.

ukberi-tibyan:36-36.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا يُؤْذَنُ لَهُمْ فَيَعْتَذِرُونَ (٣٦)).
The words of the Exalted (فَيَعْتَذِرُونَ): there are two views on its nominative. First: it is a negation like what precedes it, i.e. «فَلَا يَعْتَذِرُونَ» (so they will not excuse themselves). Second: it is resumptive (mustaʾnaf), i.e. «فَهُمْ يَعْتَذِرُونَ» (so they excuse themselves); the meaning would then be that they do not speak in a way that benefits them, i.e. they do not speak at some stations and speak at others. It is not the answer to the negation, for if it were, the nūn would have been dropped.

ukberi-tibyan:46-46.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كُلُوا وَتَمَتَّعُوا قَلِيلًا إِنَّكُمْ مُجْرِمُونَ (٤٦)).
The words of the Exalted (قَلِيلًا): i.e. a little enjoyment, or a little time. And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Mursalāt
Meccan
﷽
Abū Isḥāq said: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿والمُرْسَلاتِ عُرْفًا﴾: it has come in the exegesis that they are the winds, sent forth like the mane (ʿurf) of a horse. Likewise ﴿فالعاصِفاتِ عَصْفًا﴾ [al-Mursalāt: 2] ﴿والنّاشِراتِ نَشْرًا﴾ [al-Mursalāt: 3]: the winds that bring the rain, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي أرْسَلَ الرِّياحَ بُشْرًا بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رَحْمَتِهِ﴾ [al-Furqān: 48].

zajjaj:4-4.t: His saying: ﴿فالفارِقاتِ فَرْقًا﴾: by it the angels are meant, who brought what distinguishes between truth and falsehood. Likewise ﴿فالمُلْقِياتِ ذِكْرًا﴾ [al-Mursalāt: 5] means the angels. It was also said in the explanation of ﴿والمُرْسَلاتِ﴾ [al-Mursalāt: 1] that they are the angels sent with what is right (al-maʿrūf); and it was said that it is after the manner of a horse's mane. And it was said: ﴿فالعاصِفاتِ عَصْفًا﴾ [al-Mursalāt: 2] are the angels who snatch away the soul of the unbeliever, and the rest, to the end of the verses, also means the angels. There is a third view: ﴿والمُرْسَلاتِ عُرْفًا﴾ [al-Mursalāt: 1] means the messengers; ﴿فالعاصِفاتِ عَصْفًا﴾ [al-Mursalāt: 2] the winds; ﴿والنّاشِراتِ نَشْرًا﴾ [al-Mursalāt: 3] the winds; ﴿فالفارِقاتِ فَرْقًا﴾ — on this interpretation — the messengers again; and likewise ﴿فالمُلْقِياتِ ذِكْرًا﴾ [al-Mursalāt: 5]. All of these are in the genitive by way of oath (qasam), and the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam) is: ﴿إنَّما تُوعَدُونَ لَواقِعٌ﴾ [al-Mursalāt: 7]. One of the lexicographers said: the meaning is "By the Lord of those sent forth and of these things," as He said: ﴿فَوَرَبِّ السَّماءِ والأرْضِ إنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 23]. It was read «عَرْفًا» and «عُرْفًا», and the meaning of العُرْف and العَرْف is the same.

zajjaj:6-6.t: His saying: ﴿عُذْرًا أوْ نُذْرًا﴾ — it was also read «عُذُرًا أوْ نُذُرًا» — both have the meaning of the maṣdar (verbal noun); «اَلْعُذْرُ» and «اَلْعُذارُ» have one meaning. ﴿عُذْرًا أوْ نُذْرًا﴾ is in the accusative in two ways. One of them: as an object, by way of badal (substitute) from His saying «ذِكْرًا»; the meaning is: "and those who deliver an excuse or a warning." Or it may be accusative governed by «ذِكْرًا», so the meaning is: "and those who deliver, in that they mention an excuse or a warning." It is also possible that «عُذْرًا أوْ نُذْرًا» is accusative as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), so that the meaning is: "and those who deliver a reminder for the sake of excusing and warning."

zajjaj:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿فَإذا النُّجُومُ طُمِسَتْ﴾: its meaning is "taken away and covered over".

zajjaj:9-9.t: ﴿وَإذا السَّماءُ فُرِجَتْ﴾: its meaning is "split open", as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿إذا السَّماءُ انْشَقَّتْ﴾ [al-Inshiqāq: 1].

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿وَإذا الجِبالُ نُسِفَتْ﴾: they are taken away, all of them, swiftly. One says «اِنْتَسَفْتُ الشَّيْءَ» when you take the thing entirely and swiftly.

zajjaj:11-11.t: ﴿وَإذا الرُّسُلُ أُقِّتَتْ﴾ — it was also read «وُقِّتَتْ» with wāw, and the meaning is the same. Whoever read ﴿أُقِّتَتْ﴾ with hamza substituted the hamza for the wāw because the wāw bears ḍamma: every wāw that bears ḍamma, where its ḍamma is constant, may have a hamza substituted for it. The meaning of «وُقِّتَتْ» is: a time and a term were set for them.

zajjaj:12-12.t: His saying: ﴿لأيِّ يَوْمٍ أُجِّلَتْ﴾; then He made it clear, saying: ﴿لِيَوْمِ الفَصْلِ﴾ [al-Mursalāt: 13], that is: the judgement between them and the nations was deferred to the Day of Decision.

zajjaj:15-15.t: His saying: ﴿وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾: «وَيْلٌ» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ» is the khabar (predicate). In Arabic «وَيْلًا يَوْمَئِذٍ» would be permissible, but the readers do not permit it because it differs from the codex.

zajjaj:16-16.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ألَمْ نُهْلِكِ الأوَّلِينَ﴾ ﴿ثُمَّ نُتْبِعُهُمُ الآخِرِينَ﴾ [al-Mursalāt: 17]: this is resumptive (istiʾnāf). It is also read «ثُمَّ نُتْبِعْهُمْ» in the jussive, conjoined to «نُهْلِكِ», and the meaning is then: "Did We not destroy the former peoples", that is, first and last. Whoever reads it in the nominative takes it in the sense: "then We make the later follow the earlier, of every criminal."

zajjaj:18-18.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿كَذَلِكَ نَفْعَلُ بِالمُجْرِمِينَ﴾: the position of the kāf is accusative; the meaning is: "the like of that We do with the criminals."

zajjaj:25-26.t: His saying: ﴿ألَمْ نَجْعَلِ الأرْضَ كِفاتًا﴾ ﴿أحْياءً وأمْواتًا﴾: «كِفاتًا» means possessing gathering; the meaning is: "it holds them alive upon its back and dead in its belly." «أحْياءً» is accusative, governed by His saying ﴿كِفاتًا﴾. One says «كَفَتُّ الشَّيْءَ أكْفِتُهُ» when I gather it and draw it together. ﴿وَجَعَلْنا فِيها رَواسِيَ شامِخاتٍ﴾ [al-Mursalāt: 27], that is: firm mountains; one says «رَسا الشَّيْءُ، يَرْسُو» when it is firm. ﴿شامِخاتٍ﴾ [al-Mursalāt: 27]: lofty. ﴿وَأسْقَيْناكم ماءً فُراتًا﴾ [al-Mursalāt: 27], that is: sweet.

zajjaj:29-29.t: His saying: ﴿انْطَلِقُوا إلى ما كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تُكَذِّبُونَ﴾: the Fire is meant, because they denied the resurrection, the raising up and the Fire. ﴿انْطَلِقُوا إلى ظِلٍّ ذِي ثَلاثِ شُعَبٍ﴾ [al-Mursalāt: 30]: by "shade" here is meant the smoke of Hell. Then He, Mighty and Majestic, made known that it gives no shade and repels nothing of the flame of the Fire, saying: ﴿لا ظَلِيلٍ ولا يُغْنِي مِنَ اللَّهَبِ﴾ [al-Mursalāt: 31]. ﴿إنَّها تَرْمِي بِشَرَرٍ كالقَصْرِ﴾ [al-Mursalāt: 32]: it has come in the exegesis that it is a palace (qaṣr) of these palaces. It was also said: «اَلْقَصْرُ» is the plural of «قَصَرَةٌ», which is the thick part of trees. It was also read «كالقَصَرِ» with fatḥa on the ṣād, plural of «قَصَرَةٌ», that is: as though they were the necks of camels.

zajjaj:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿كَأنَّهُ جِمالَتٌ صُفْرٌ﴾: it is read «جِمالَت» and «جُمالاتٌ», with ḍamma and kasra on the jīm. It means that the sparks are like black camels; camels that are black tending towards yellow are called «إبِلٌ صُفْرٌ» ("yellow camels"). Whoever read «جِمالَت» with kasra made it the plural of «جِمالٌ», as you say «بُيُوتٌ» and «بُيُوتاتٌ»; it is the plural of a plural. Whoever read «جُمالاتٌ» with ḍamma made it the plural of «جُمالَةٌ», which is a thick rope (qals) of the ropes of seagoing ships; and it is said: like a rope of the ropes of a bridge. It may also be the plural of «جَمَلٌ»: «جِمالٌ» and «جُمالاتٌ», as «رِجالٌ» is said as the plural of «رَجُلٌ». It was also read «جِمالَت صُفْرٌ» as a plural of «جَمَلٌ», «جِمالَةٌ», as one says «حَجَرٌ» and «حِجارَةٌ», «ذَكَرٌ» and «ذِكارَةٌ». And it was read «جُمالَةٌ صُفْرٌ», according to what we explained for «جُمالاتٌ».
«[Translator's note: the readings named in this entry («جِمالَت», «جُمالاتٌ», «جِمالَةٌ», «جُمالَةٌ») are printed exactly as in the source, whose vocalisation of them is not fully consistent.]»

zajjaj:35-36.t: His saying: ﴿هَذا يَوْمُ لا يَنْطِقُونَ﴾ ﴿وَلا يُؤْذَنُ لَهم فَيَعْتَذِرُونَ﴾: the Day of Resurrection has stations and appointed times, and this is one of the appointed times in which they do not speak.

zajjaj:38-38.t: His saying: ﴿هَذا يَوْمُ الفَصْلِ﴾, that is: this is a day on which judgement is made between the people of the Garden and of the Fire, and the people of truth and of falsehood.

zajjaj:43-43.t: His saying: ﴿كُلُوا واشْرَبُوا هَنِيئًا بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾: here a verb of saying is implied; the meaning is: "The God-fearing are amid shades and springs and fruits such as they desire; it is said to them: Eat and drink with relish for what you used to do."

zajjaj:48-48.t: His saying: ﴿وَإذا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ارْكَعُوا لا يَرْكَعُونَ﴾: when they were commanded to pray, they did not pray.

zajjaj:50-50.t: His saying: ﴿فَبِأيِّ حَدِيثٍ بَعْدَهُ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾, that is: so in what discourse, after the Qur'an — which came to them containing clear explanation, and which is a miracle and an abiding sign, a proof of Islam, among what the Prophet, upon him be peace, brought — will they believe?!
